#225348. What music sells a house? Agents say it’s not about genre

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1522 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Inman ↗ Open Full Page

What music sells a house? Agents say it’s not about genre

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1522 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that taylor Swift, classical or silence?
  • Ask real estate agents what soundtrack sells a house, and you’ll get two answers.
  • Inman asked agents and brokers from Manhattan to Breckenridge, Colorado, and they described the music they play at showings and open houses and how they match it to the property.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that taylor Swift, classical or silence? Agents explain how they pick open house music, the one rule most follow and why none can prove it works.

Ask real estate agents what soundtrack sells a house, and you’ll get two answers. One is a carefully curated playlist, while the other is silence.

Inman asked agents and brokers from Manhattan to Breckenridge, Colorado, and they described the music they play at showings and open houses and how they match it to the property.

Recent findings suggest that none could point to hard numbers showing a playlist moved a home faster or for more money. What they did offer was a clear set of rules from the agents who use music, and an equally firm argument from those who won’t touch it.

Ben Jacobs, co-founder of the Chestler Jacobs Team at Douglas Elliman in New York City, thinks music raises more questions than it answers. He said he’s not a fan of playing music during showings.

“Buyers may wonder if the agent is trying to mask something, whether it’s street noise, construction nearby, sounds within the building or even a noisy appliance,” Jacobs told Inman. “You want buyers to experience the home as it actually is, without anything distracting from their ability to evaluate the space.”.

Recent findings suggest that his co-founder, Jessica Chestler, mentioned music has its place. That place is just not a private showing.

“Music can be wonderful for setting a mood at a cocktail party, listing launch or special event, but during a showing, I think there’s something to be said for letting the property speak for itself,” Chestler said.

Industry observers note that megan Sullivan works at the same brokerage, and she uses music for the very reason Jacobs avoids it. Sullivan sells large estate homes across Fairfield and Westchester counties out of Douglas Elliman’s Greenwich, Connecticut, office. Some of those homes sit within earshot of things a seller can’t fix.

It has been revealed that “I actually do like incorporating music into certain showings, particularly when a property is impacted by outside noise from planes, trains or automobiles,” Sullivan said. “Thoughtfully selected background music can help create a more welcoming atmosphere and soften those distractions, allowing buyers to focus on the overall experience of the home. I think it’s very property-specific.”.

Jeffrey Hensel is a broker associate with North Coast Financial, a California hard money lender that funds fix-and-flip and probate deals. He looks at it from the investor side.

“Dead silence can amplify every creak, clank, and drip in an otherwise quiet home,” he mentioned. “Background music masks these sounds and provides some white noise to help set a calm mood.”.

Sources indicate that agents in the pro-music camp mostly aren’t trying to cover anything up. They simply want buyers to stay longer.

Sandra Daniels of Harry Norman, Realtors | Forbes Global Properties serves the East Cobb and Marietta area outside Atlanta. She’s currently listing a $3.9 million estate in The River Club in Suwanee, Georgia.

For those showings, she rotates light classical piano, The Macarons Project and a Spotify playlist called “Nora Ephron + Nancy Meyers Dinner Party.”.

“Put a buyer in a home with a glass of Champagne or a cup of coffee and the right music playing, and that cozy, inviting atmosphere encourages people to stay, relax and feel at home,” Daniels told Inman.

Recent findings suggest that daniels also has a low-tech trick for vacant listings she expects to sell in the first week. She bought an old-school CD player and a few classical CDs. She leaves it on repeat through the first weekend of showings and stops by each evening to turn off the lights and music and lock up.

Natalia Bassova, founder and CEO of Resort Real Estate in Breckenridge, Colorado, saw the same effect at a luxury mountain listing. The home looked great, she noted, but it demonstrated cold.

“By adding some background instrumental music, it gave the buyers more time to spend in the home. They spent more time in the kitchen and great room areas,” Bassova said. “The property didn’t change, but the atmosphere did.”.

For mountain and luxury homes, Bassova plays acoustic and piano music, including Ludovico Einaudi and The Piano Guys. For condos and newly introduced construction, she switches to soft contemporary instrumentals.

Agents who play music disagree on genre, but almost all agree on one thing: avoid lyrics.

Industry observers note that “If the buyer begins to think about the music, then it is having a negative impact,” Bassova said. Her never-play list covers anything with strong lyrics, politics, swearing or heavy bass.

In a recent development, andrea Seeney is a global real estate advisor with Atlanta Fine Homes Sotheby’s International Realty and a trained opera singer and classical pianist. She compared lyrics to a seller’s personal effects.

“Acoustic performances are best because they set a tone and allow the buyer to fill in the blanks with their own thoughts,” Seeney said.

She leans toward jazz and usually plays Spotify’s Coffee House radio or its Ella Fitzgerald playlist. She says music works on buyers through memory: a song can take someone back to a time and place they enjoyed, “and that memory then reflects positively on the home.”.

According to recent reports, hensel takes the lyrics rule a step further, to genre itself. If an agent plays hip-hop or country for a buyer who doesn’t listen to it, he says, that signals an assumption about who the buyer is. That can create friction neither side notices. His pick is quiet cocktail-lounge jazz like Miles Davis or Bill Evans, at a steady tempo and volume.

According to recent reports, he also cited retail research by psychological scientists Adrian North and Lorraine Sheridan of Curtin University and Charles Areni of Macquarie University. It found that shoppers who heard classical music rated merchandise as higher quality and were willing to spend more.

Some agents ignore the rulebook completely.

In a recent development, rachel Kilmer, an agent with ReeceNichols Real Estate in Kansas City, Missouri, plays Taylor Swift at nearly every open house. She swaps in country for more rural listings.

“In Kansas City, she’s a conversation starter,” Kilmer stated. “People come in, and it’s, ‘Are you a Swiftie?’ ‘No, but I love the Chiefs!’ It really helps loosen up the conversation.”.

She added, “I’m the one sitting there listening to it for two hours!”.

Monica Shea, a broker with KW Aspire in Colorado Springs, Colorado, builds whole open houses around a theme, and the music follows.

She played the Eras Tour set list at a Taylor Swift–themed open house and the Frozen soundtrack at a hot cocoa bar event. A Halloween open house got not-too-spooky Halloween music. For regular showings, she has sellers put on a YouTube channel with seasonal background music and scenery.

It has been revealed that shea’s never-play list puts her directly at odds with a few other agents: smooth jazz. Shea says she never plays “anything that sounds like the Weather Channel.”.

Marcel Finkelstein of Team BlackStar at eXp Realty hosts open houses every Sunday across Monmouth County, New Jersey. He sees music as more of an icebreaker than a staging tool.

His Apple Music rotation includes lounge instrumentals, vocal-free dance-pop and Bon Entendeur. It also has Afro house from DJ Alex Niyazov and the warm trumpet and sax of Fausto Papetti and Paul Mauriat.

He uses the same approach whether the listing is a $600,000 two-bedroom condo in Manalapan or a $2 million six-bedroom in Colts Neck.

“I want the atmosphere to feel calm, comfortable and welcoming, rather than like a sales presentation,” Finkelstein stated.

Finkelstein added that his Instagram followers also know how much he loves music.

“Every week, I share new songs and incorporate music into my stories and posts about homes,” he remarked. “It’s a personal interest that carries through into how I present properties.”.

It has been revealed that on setup, agents who play music give similar advice. Keep the volume low enough that buyers can ask questions and the agent can hear their feedback. Use one good speaker rather than several.

Industry observers note that bassova puts hers in the middle of the home, and Seeney puts a small Bluetooth speaker in the kitchen. When sellers have a Sonos system, Daniels connects to it from her MacBook or iPad. Otherwise, she brings her own Bose speaker.

Recent findings suggest that kilmer runs her music from an iPad instead of her phone. “That way, incoming calls and texts don’t interrupt the music,” she said.

As for proof, none of the agents Inman spoke with track music as a performance metric. Bassova remarked she gets buyer feedback that certain homes feel relaxing, but nothing tied to days on market or offers.

In a recent development, so the evidence is anecdotal, and the playlists don’t agree. Agents can’t even settle on jazz. Both camps share one goal: the buyer should notice the home, not the soundtrack.

As Bassova mentioned, “If the buyer begins to think about the music, then it is having a negative impact.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Alan Boyle on Nov 19, 2026 at 7:00 amNovember 19, 2026 at 8:01 am.
  • Zeno Power has hit a major milestone in its push to build nuclear batteries for underwater use.
  • Recent findings suggest that the startup said today that it successfully demonstrated an electrically heated Stirling generator in a controlled maritime setting in Washington state.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Alan Boyle on Nov 19, 2026 at 7:00 amNovember 19, 2026 at 8:01 am.

Zeno Power has hit a major milestone in its push to build nuclear batteries for underwater use.

Recent findings suggest that the startup said today that it successfully demonstrated an electrically heated Stirling generator in a controlled maritime setting in Washington state. The two-week demonstration produced electrical power outputs in excess of 20 watts, said Lindsey Boles, Zeno’s chief product officer.

“It’s a really big step for us — just solidifying our expertise in how to design these, and then confirming our ability to translate that into operational hardware that meets or exceeds what our customers need,” Boles told GeekWire.

Sources indicate that zeno is developing the power system with support from the Department of Defense as a follow-up to an initial $7.5 million contract awarded in 2023. The generator uses a Stirling engine to convert heat into electricity by cycling gas through heating and cooling phases in a closed cylinder.

According to recent reports, for the recent demonstration, the prototype device relied on an electric heating element. Future devices will instead rely on heat generated by the radioactive decay of strontium-90, a radioisotope that can be extracted from spent nuclear fuel.

In a recent development, nuclear batteries have been in use for decades, primarily for space missions ranging from the Apollo moon shots to NASA’s Voyager spacecraft and Mars rovers. But the batteries being developed by Zeno Power promise to be at least four times more efficient than traditional radioisotope thermoelectric generators, Boles said.

Recent findings suggest that boles said the non-radiological test exceeded expectations. “There’s a difference between a design that works on paper and hardware that works in the field,” she said in a news release. “This is the moment our team has been building toward: proof that this technology works outside the lab.”.

Long-lasting nuclear batteries could be used to power undersea sensor networks or recharge autonomous underwater vehicles. “There are a lot of applications, especially on the maritime front, that we really want electricity for,” Boles stated. “And we really don’t need a ton of it. But we need it to be really reliable, and we need it to be long endurance, and we need it to be self-managed. … I think of it like a slow Tesla supercharger on the seabed.”.

According to recent reports, retired Navy Adm. John Richardson, former chief of naval operations and a member of Zeno’s board of directors, called the recent test an “crucial step toward undersea superiority.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Protecting maritime infrastructure and powering distributed systems at sea requires energy; energy that lasts for years, not days or months,” Richardson stated in a written statement. “As competition intensifies in contested domains, powered subsea systems will help keep us ahead. Zeno Power has steadily reduced risk, proven its technology, built a supply chain, and prepared to scale production.”.

Sources indicate that next year, Zeno Power plans to install a radioisotope heat source in its generator and test the system in a water tank under controlled laboratory conditions. If those tests are successful, Zeno will move forward with the first operational seabed deployment of its radioisotope-fueled maritime system later in 2027.

Recent findings suggest that the maritime battery isn’t Zeno’s only product. The manufacturer is also working on a nuclear-powered heater system for spacecraft, with a demonstration on the lunar surface planned as early as 2028. Zeno’s broader vision is to provide long-lasting, reliable power on the moon and Mars, and in extreme environments on Earth.

Industry observers note that since its founding in 2018, Zeno has secured $105 million in private capital and has brought in $60 million in contracts with the Pentagon and NASA. The firm has more than 95 employees at locations in Seattle, California and Washington, D.C., with the largest contingent working at its engineering headquarters in Seattle’s South Lake Union district.

UPDATED 16:13 EST / NOVEMBER 26 2026.

According to recent reports, an investigation has shed light on links between some Nvidia Corp. partners and companies that are based in China or are accused of breaching export controls.

According to recent reports, the analysis was carried out by C4ADS, a Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit, at the request of CBS News. The outlet published the findings Wednesday evening.

The first focus of the investigation was a San Jose, California-based manufacturer called RiCloud AI Inc. It’s an Nvidia preferred partner, which means that it can buy the chipmaker’s high-end graphics processing units. Companies with that partner destination also have access to Nvidia’s GPU software and technical support services.

According to recent reports, the investigation determined that RiCloud AI is a unit of Shenzen-based Yuxing InfoTech Investment Holdings Ltd. The latter manufacturer’s chief executive reportedly has a degree from a university run by China’s military. Yuxing’s chair, in turn, previously worked at a Chinese tech firm that drew national security scrutiny in Australia.

RiCloud AI recently signed a $120 million deal to lease Nvidia-powered servers to a Taiwanese whiskey tech giant. The latter firm generated just $609,000 in profits last year.

It has been revealed that the investigation also looked into a company called Topmost Corp. It’s reportedly linked to a California businessman who was recently indicted for allegedly smuggling GPUs to China.

In a recent development, according to CBS News, Topmost’s website states that it’s an authorized reseller of Nvidia partner 2CRSi Inc. The latter tech giant makes servers powered by the chipmaker’s GPUs. Last month, it disclosed that it received a grand jury subpoena in connection with a client “we ourselves had reported to the authorities.”.

It has been revealed that the report also noted that California-based Aivres Inc. has exported $3 billion worth of Nvidia-powered servers to Southeast Asia since 2024. It’s a subsidiary of Inspur, a Chinese tech firm that is on the U.S. Commerce Department’s Entity List. Organizations on the list are subject to trade restrictions.

Sources indicate that U.S. regulations prohibit companies from exporting Nvidia’s most advanced GPUs to China. Earlier this month, the Commerce Department closed a loophole that Chinese tech firms used to bypass those restrictions. The tech firms in questions rented access to Nvidia GPUs deployed in data centers outside China.

It has been revealed that some of the data centers used by Chinese companies are in Southeast Asia. On Wednesday, the Financial Times reported that Nvidia had instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping GPU-equipped servers to four countries in the region. It’s reportedly unclear whether the move is temporary.

Separately, CNBC reported that companies have put an “unusually high” number of Nvidia GPUs up for sale since the Commerce Department declared the new restrictions. It’s believed the chips were intended for data centers that are used by Chinese firms. According to the report, thousands of high-end B300 GPUs are among the processors that were put up for sale.

  • Homeownership is slipping further out of reach for young Americans, according to the National Association of Realtors’ 2026 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that congratulations, you’ve made it to Friday again this week. But before you head out for the weekend, we’re bringing you a quick catch-up on the biggest headlines and the most helpful how-tos for your business. So, Take 5 and peruse our top editor picks for this week and why they matter to your business.

According to recent reports, P.S. Don’t miss The Download, our weekly column that breaks down one of the week’s top stories and equips you with what you’ll need to meet next Monday head-on.

Homeownership is slipping further out of reach for young Americans, according to the National Association of Realtors’ 2026 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers. The report, released on Thursday, revealed that the share of first-time homebuyers rose 1 percent year over year to 22 percent. Despite the small gain, first-time buyer activity remains near historic lows (21 percent) and 18 percentage points below pre-2008 trends (40 percent). Same as last year, the median age of a first-time homebuyer was 40 — roughly a decade older than the typical median age in the 1980s.

Why it matters: This annual report gives you a pulse on national real estate trends and how you might want to pivot your strategies. For example, as noted above, the median age of the first-time homebuyer is 40, and the share of single women homeowners has risen to 20 percent. A longer nurture campaign might be in order (ahem, see below), and if you’re not already marketing toward single women, perhaps you should. Read the full report for more.

EXTRA: The buyer who can’t close for a year is your best asset in 2026.

AI has been the topic of conversation for the past couple of years. And there’s a lot of talk. So how do you suss through the noise and find what works for your business? Jimmy Burgess has created a no-nonsense list of seven AI tools that are actually worth your time.

In a recent development, why it matters: Burgess shares not only his top tools but also how to use them. These tools will help you turn prompts into better questions, find the questions your future clients are asking, remember the details that matter, evaluate your AI search visibility, turn one video into multiple pieces of content, make video editing easier and use AI as a strategist rather than a writing assistant. Don’t feel overwhelmed. You don’t have to use all of them at once.

Krystopher Benyamein recently sold a property in San Pedro where his team hosted nine open houses, mailed 500 postcards, ran digital advertising and created a video that generated more than 1.5 million organic views. They found a buyer and opened escrow, but shortly before closing, that buyer backed out, and they had to start again.

They eventually found another buyer and successfully closed, but when they shared the case study on Instagram, they didn’t lead with the sale price or how much marketing they’d done. They opened with, “Imagine finally selling your house. Then the buyer backs out right before closing.”.

Sources indicate that that opening puts the reader in the seller’s position. Most homeowners can imagine how frustrating that experience would be, and it naturally creates curiosity about what happened next. From there, they explained how they responded, got the property back in front of buyers and ultimately closed.

According to recent reports, why it matters: In today’s market, there are many stories of buyers backing out of deals. This approach allows you to create content that keeps you top of mind, show sellers exactly how you work and reach a wider audience. Benyamein reveals you how to do it and shares a FREE Canva template to help get the job done.

VA loans often get passed over for conventional loans. Inman’s Nick Pipitone spoke with Fathom Realty’s Lindsey Schmidt, an Army veteran who served in Iraq, about why VA financing still carries a stigma among sellers and listing agents, how she gets around it and why VA assumptions remain one of the most misunderstood tools in the market.

Why it matters: Military members often have to move. Understanding and busting myths about VA loans can help you get ahead of objections before making an offer, which will help you get more deals across the finish line and get more service members into homes.

Compass has been busy, creating and formalizing policy around employees in association leadership positions and how Compass brokerage agents cooperate on private listings.

The organization unveiled Thursday that it is filing 15 federal antitrust lawsuits against MLSs across eight states, accusing the organizations of illegally restricting how agents can publicly market homes outside their systems. Compass alleges that the MLSs unlawfully fine agents for publicly marketing listings outside the MLS, with penalties it notes can reach $15,000.

Why it matters: Compass International Holdings is presently in litigation with 16 total MLSs across 18 federal lawsuits. Not only is this massive news that’s making waves throughout the industry, but its ripple effects could impact your MLS’s rules, if they haven’t already.

EXTRA: What Compass’ leadership ban signals for agents and associations.

Amazon’s $18B bet on Anthropic tops $200B, for a moment, in the Claude maker’s historic market debut

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (575 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 19, 2026 at 9:54 amNovember 19, 2026 at 10:10 am.
  • Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut today in a record $81.3 billion initial public offering, with big financial stakes for the Seattle area’s two tech giants.
  • For Amazon, the IPO is a paper windfall.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 19, 2026 at 9:54 amNovember 19, 2026 at 10:10 am.

Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut today in a record $81.3 billion initial public offering, with big financial stakes for the Seattle area’s two tech giants.

For Amazon, the IPO is a paper windfall. The company started putting money into Anthropic in 2023, about $18 billion in all. At the $83 IPO price, its stake was worth about $161 billion. With Anthropic opening at $111.50 a share, that number was closer to $216 billion. The stock has since dropped below $100, which put Amazon’s stake under $200 billion.

Beyond the value of the investment, Anthropic is a major customer for Amazon’s cloud platform. The Claude maker has committed to spend at least $110 billion on Amazon Web Services through 2036.

For Microsoft, it’s more complicated. The Redmond firm agreed in late 2025 to invest up to $5 billion but hasn’t disclosed the size of its stake. Microsoft is buying $1 billion of Anthropic stock alongside the IPO, one of seven tech companies buying a combined $26 billion. Anthropic has committed to spend at least $47 billion on Microsoft’s Azure cloud through 2033.

But Microsoft is also pitching its own AI models against Anthropic’s, and it has been working to replace Anthropic’s models with OpenAI’s in some Copilot features, The Information reported this week.

Industry observers note that listing Anthropic’s compute partners on CNBC this morning, co-founder Daniela Amodei named Nvidia, Amazon, Google and Broadcom, but not Microsoft. Whether it was a slip or something more significant, it was an interesting omission.

A historic debut: The offering tops SpaceX’s $75 billion IPO in June, and it makes Anthropic the first standalone AI lab to go public, ahead of OpenAI.

In a recent development, the five-year-old manufacturer was valued at about $1.5 trillion at the $83 IPO price, on a fully diluted basis that counts employee stock and other shares not yet issued. The stock opened at $111.50, valuing Anthropic at about $2 trillion on the same basis. It has since traded as low as about $95.

Speaking before the opening bell, CEO Dario Amodei said Anthropic will slow the training and release of its AI models for as long as it takes to be confident they’re safe, and that going public only strengthens that resolve.

“We will not bend to either business nor political pressure,” he remarked.

In an interview with CNBC’s Andrew Ross Sorkin afterward, Amodei called the push and pull between growth and that kind of restraint “one of the central tensions at the heart of the firm.”.

Anthropic is also a public benefit corporation, a structure that legally requires the organization to balance shareholders’ interests with the public good.

Industry observers note that what’s next: Both Seattle-area giants have hedged their bets. Microsoft owns about 24% of OpenAI, and Amazon put $50 billion into OpenAI earlier this year.

OpenAI, which confidentially filed for its own IPO in June, is still aiming to go public in 2027.

Anthropic’s co-founders and some of its biggest shareholders are barred from selling for up to a year under the IPO’s lock-up rules, and Amazon has stated it expects a customary lock-up period.

Amazon will upgrade the value of its Anthropic holdings in its fourth-quarter results, much of it through earnings, which means the paper windfall is likely to boost Amazon’s fourth-quarter profit even though it hasn’t sold a share.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • McInerney, president and CEO of Genworth Financial, has stepped down from his roles at the company and its board of directors to focus on his health, the company confirmed.
  • Fannie Mae appointed David Shafer to its board of directors effective Nov.
  • It has been revealed that the manufacturer also entered into retention agreements with four executives totaling $4.75 million.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas J. McInerney, president and CEO of Genworth Financial, has stepped down from his roles at the company and its board of directors to focus on his health, the company confirmed. The board appointed Jerome T. Upton, its current chief financial officer, as president, CEO and director. Upton will remain CFO through Dec. 31, with Angela Simmons expected to assume the role on Jan. 1, 2027.

Fannie Mae appointed David Shafer to its board of directors effective Nov. 23. His term will end at the next annual board election, or if he resigns or is removed by the Federal Housing Finance Agency. His committee assignments have not yet been determined.

It has been revealed that the manufacturer also entered into retention agreements with four executives totaling $4.75 million. Chief financial officer Chryssa Halley and chief investment officer Erik Bisso will each receive $1.5 million, multifamily executive vice president Kelly Follain will receive $1 million, and chief risk officer Anthony Moon will receive $750,000.

The awards will be paid in two equal installments, in December 2026 and December 2027, provided the executives remain employed and comply with the agreements, according to filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

According to recent reports, the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York elected Charles E. Kilbourne, managing director of the Financial Services Volunteer Corps and an independent director since 2019, as board chair for a two-year term beginning Jan. 1, 2027. Kilbourne, who chairs the board’s housing committee, will succeed Chris Martin, who is retiring at the end of this year after more than a decade of service.

In a recent development, element Home Loans, a division of NFM Lending, has hired Darrell Boan as branch manager in Greensboro, North Carolina, as the company expands its presence in the Southeast. Boan, who has more than 25 years of mortgage industry experience, will lead local growth, support loan originators, and build relationships with clients and community partners.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Renowned financial guru and Rich Dad Poor Dad author Robert Kiyosaki has offered compelling insight into the reasons behind his buying spree of Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH) despite the current crypto market crash.

Kiyosaki, who is an esteemed investor, predicts that a financial crisis could be on the horizon, and it might be even worse than the 2008 market crash. He believes that crypto assets and other hard assets are an effective hedge against the repercussions of government-induced overborrowing and money printing.

The financial guru's latest X post explains his rationale behind investing in Bitcoin, Ethereum, gold, silver, real estate, and oil instead of traditional financial assets.

"Why I am buying real (no ETFs) gold, silver, Bitcoin, and Ethereum," Kiyosaki noted in his latest post.

It has been revealed that he attributed his views to the Federal Reserve, the U.S. Treasury and the colossal debt obligations of the U.S.

According to Kiyosaki, the government's inability to curb spending will lead to massive money printing in the future. This might erode the purchasing power of the U.S. dollar.

"The BIG PRINT is about to begin," Kiyosaki warned.

This is the core reason for his investments in Bitcoin and Ethereum. He believes that these assets will rise in value when the government is forced to aggressively print money in response to escalating financial problems.

Moreover, he believes that holding these crypto assets directly would be better than investing in exchange-traded funds (ETFs). However, he did not offer a reason for his opposition to ETFs in his post.

Furthermore, Kiyosaki stated that the next financial crisis could be much bigger than the global financial crisis of 2008.

Recent findings suggest that "This crash we are just now sliding into is much bigger than 2008. Possibly a global depression," he commented.

He also mentioned that his gold, silver, Bitcoin and Ethereum holdings could make him one of the ultra-rich if his predictions come true.

Recent findings suggest that however, Kiyosaki mentioned some figures that were not entirely accurate. For instance, he stated that the U.S. national debt stood at $49 trillion. But according to Treasury data, the national debt was about $40.7 trillion in November 2026. Also, his claim that the U.S. is printing $1 trillion every 90 days conflates government debt with money printing.

Although Kiyosaki is a strong believer in Bitcoin, he recently advised investors not to buy Bitcoin immediately amid the digital asset's current price slump.

On Nov. 20, the Rich Dad Poor Dad author cautioned against catching a 'falling knife.'.

"Never grab a falling knife." This means that investors should wait for the market crash to end before buying.

"I started buying bitcoin around $20k after the market crashed last time," Kiyosaki recalled.

"Will wait for Bitcoin bottom again," he added.

NAR saved for his $541K exit; now it won’t pay, ex-CFO indicates

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (819 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Former National Association of Realtors Chief Financial Officer John Pierpoint has sued the organization for unpaid retirement compensation totaling more than $541,000, according to a complaint filed on Tuesday.
  • Recent findings suggest that pierpoint alleged NAR has paid senior vice presidents one year of their base salary at retirement since 2005.
  • Recent findings suggest that pierpoint retired from NAR on March 31, 2025 — a date he chose with the 2023 Sitzer | Burnett buyer-broker commission lawsuit in mind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former National Association of Realtors Chief Financial Officer John Pierpoint has sued the organization for unpaid retirement compensation totaling more than $541,000, according to a complaint filed on Tuesday.

Recent findings suggest that pierpoint alleged NAR has paid senior vice presidents one year of their base salary at retirement since 2005. To avoid booking the full expense when a senior vice president retired, NAR created a Compensation Reserve that let it steadily set aside funds throughout the executive’s tenure, which it would release at retirement. Pierpoint helped establish the reserve in 2005 at the direction of former NAR CEO Dale Stinton, court documents said.

Recent findings suggest that pierpoint retired from NAR on March 31, 2025 — a date he chose with the 2023 Sitzer | Burnett buyer-broker commission lawsuit in mind. The former CFO remarked he was key in executing the buyer-broker commission settlement payout, which totaled $418 million. The first settlement payment, totaling roughly $200 million, was issued in February 2025, with subsequent payments of $72 million per year until the full $418 million is paid.

Pierpoint mentioned he notified NAR of his impending retirement in late 2024 and requested his retirement payout. However, six days before his last day with NAR, Pierpoint alleged that a Grant Thornton auditor named White — there is no first name listed in the court documents — emailed him and said that “NAR had been ‘unable to locate any policy or verify any consistent practice’ concerning the Compensation Reserve or ‘the payout to executives of a full year of salary upon retirement.'”.

According to recent reports, white also allegedly stated that the Compensation Reserve “was not used to fund” the exit packages of eight other senior vice presidents who retired before Pierpoint, which are listed in the court documents as L.J., F.S., B.M., D.H., J.G.,  J.B., D.G. and B.G. Real Estate News said L.J., D.G. and B.G. are likely former general counsel Laurie Janik, former SVP of talent development and resources Donna Gland, and former senior vice president and CEO Bob Goldberg.

As a result, Grant Thornton noted it was “unable to approve the payout of a full year’s compensation without any concrete proof that such act is mandated by an employment agreement, policy or proposal.”.

Pierpoint claimed NAR had the funds to pay his retirement benefit and provided a ledger outlining what the Association allegedly reserved from December 2014 to December 2024. He also mentioned the trial balances NAR provided to outside auditors, including Grant Thornton, included evidence of the Compensation Reserve’s existence and purpose.

It has been revealed that “NAR carried its obligation to Pierpoint at approximately 97.6 cents on the dollar three months before it refused to pay him anything,” the complaint read. “The practice NAR now claims it cannot verify is documented in NAR’s own ledger, its own year-end schedules, its own payroll records and its own audit files, and was paid to every one of Pierpoint’s predecessors who retired. NAR did not stop believing in its obligation; it stopped wanting to pay it.”.

Visualized with the help of AI.

In a recent development, pierpoint’s counsel accused NAR of shirking its obligation to pay the former CFO due to its financial woes after the settlement. In December 2025, former NAR president Kevin Sears stated the buyer-broker commission settlement saved the Association’s finances — the other option was to file an appeal and declare bankruptcy.

Sources indicate that “John Pierpoint helped guide NAR through an extraordinarily challenging period in its history, including the financial consequences of the antitrust litigation,” said David Fish, an attorney with Workplace Law Partners, P.C., who represents Pierpoint. “After nearly four decades of service, he expected the organization to honor the same retirement compensation practice it had followed for other senior executives.”.

“We believe the evidence will establish that the financial pressures following the antitrust verdict did not relieve NAR of its obligation to pay compensation earned by its employees,” he added.

Sources indicate that pierpoint’s counsel is requesting that NAR pay the $541,059 retirement payout, statutory damages of 5 percent of the unpaid amount for each month it remains unpaid, attorneys’ fees and costs, and prejudgment and post-judgment interest. They also seek a jury trial.

NAR denied Pierpoint’s claims, saying that the former CFO has “[mischaracterized] a varied set of individual arrangements with departing executives as a uniform and guaranteed retirement benefit.”.

Sources indicate that “Mr. Pierpoint was not entitled to the payment he now seeks, and NAR’s decision was unrelated to its antitrust settlement or its financial condition,” an NAR spokesperson told Inman in an emailed statement. “NAR is committed to appropriate financial controls and responsible stewardship of its members’ dues dollars. NAR pays compensation and benefits that are actually owed, not just because a former executive requests payment. No such obligation exists here, and we intend to vigorously defend against these claims through the appropriate legal process.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 19, 2026 at 10:07 amNovember 24, 2026 at 9:53 am.
  • It has been revealed that editor’s note: This series profiles five Seattle-area “Uncommon Thinkers,” who will be recognized Dec.
  • Andrew Redd‘s career path creates a tidy narrative: grow up in Seattle steeped in aviation and maritime culture, study mechanical engineering and aerospace, work at SpaceX, then launch an offshore geothermal energy startup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 19, 2026 at 10:07 amNovember 24, 2026 at 9:53 am.

It has been revealed that editor’s note: This series profiles five Seattle-area “Uncommon Thinkers,” who will be recognized Dec. 10 at the GeekWire Gala in partnership with Greater Seattle Partners.

Andrew Redd‘s career path creates a tidy narrative: grow up in Seattle steeped in aviation and maritime culture, study mechanical engineering and aerospace, work at SpaceX, then launch an offshore geothermal energy startup.

The dots connect, but the picture they form is anything but ordinary: bold in vision, fast in execution and enormous in potential.

Redd has next-level ambition, and he’s directing it at solving one of the world’s biggest and most urgent problems — adding renewable, massively scalable energy that can outcompete fossil fuels and reach the grid rapidly enough to make a difference in the race against climate change.

Recent findings suggest that underwater geothermal energy has never been tapped in a significant way, but to Redd, the idea was irresistible. “It checks all of the boxes for our perfect future energy source,” he remarked.

In a recent development, he founded Endurance Energy on the north shore of Seattle’s Lake Union in January 2025, and this September the team oversaw its fifth deep-sea deployment. At a site 300 miles off the Oregon coast, its prototype system generated more electricity than it consumed. The startup has raised $63 million from investors and has roughly three dozen employees.

Nate Bek, a principal at Ascend, praised Redd’s ability to attract “brilliant” talent in pursuit of his goal. The Seattle venture firm is one of the startup’s early backers.

Sources indicate that “I’ve been deeply inspired by what [Redd]’s building at Endurance and haven’t shut up about it since the day we met,” Bek stated. “He somehow makes powering the world from the bottom of the ocean feel inevitable, all while remaining remarkably measured and transparent about the progress.”.

For Redd, studying engineering and aerospace in college was so clear-cut that it wasn’t a choice at all. Growing up around Boeing, seaplanes, the Museum of Flight and the Pacific Northwest’s rich maritime industry naturally pointed him toward those sectors. He wanted a degree as expansive as his influences.

“I didn’t really want to have to choose whether it was going to be boats or space travel or airplanes,” he said. “I just wanted to be able to do anything — keep the world as wide open as possible.”.

Sources indicate that after graduating from Princeton University, Redd worked at Neuralink, an Elon Musk firm developing technology that lets the brain communicate directly with computers. A year later, in 2021, he moved to Musk’s rocket company, SpaceX.

That was another no-duh decision, as Redd viewed it.

According to recent reports, “I saw SpaceX as really the place to be, where early-career people are given the most amount of resources and responsibility, and that felt like the fastest way to learn and the most engaging possible scenario to be in,” Redd stated. “I wanted to be tossed into something that was a little bit crazy.”.

Redd joined as SpaceX was starting to build its first orbital Starship rockets. The program brought together passionate young people and experienced SpaceX engineers who served as mentors. Wild ideas were entertained and explored. Everyone was committed to the mission. It was just the experience Redd wanted, and he planned to stick around for seven to 10 years.

Then artificial intelligence started booming.

In 2024, the build-out of sprawling, energy-hungry data centers for AI was accelerating with no end in sight. At the same time, efforts to electrify transportation, heating and cooling were driving up demand for power. Redd saw these trends sparking a surge in latest natural gas generation, locking in decades of carbon emissions.

He wanted to find a better way. He went into engineering mode, focusing on all the essential criteria for an energy source: it had to be clean, not dependent on intermittent sun or wind, capable of producing massive amounts of energy, readily deployable, subject to fewer regulatory hurdles than something like nuclear, economically competitive, and scalable.

Industry observers note that redd recognized the tremendous heat contained under Earth’s surface as a terrific source for renewable energy and realized that most of the world’s active volcanoes are offshore. The unknown was whether the rocky ocean floor would be suitable for geothermal wells, so he did some research and found publications from geology experts who noted the conditions would be “perfect.”.

“You can tell,” he said, “when there’s a moment in time that you need to go and reach out and grab something, and that was really my impression — if I didn’t start this now, this would never come into existence, or wouldn’t come into existence soon enough to make a meaningful impact.”.

In launching Endurance, Redd was intentional about the culture he wanted to create. He was aiming for a multidisciplinary group of mission-driven employees eager to collaborate and learn from each other: top talent that would attract more of the same and make Endurance a place people were excited to work.

“The hardest part of an early-stage startup is recruiting,” Redd noted, “especially if you’re a first-time founder.”.

The startup employs about a dozen SpaceX alumni, plus employees from the fusion organization Helion Energy and the aerospace venture Blue Origin.

A strong team is key to Endurance’s success. That’s because, enthusiasm and passion aside, the startup faces steep engineering and economic challenges. The technology must withstand high pressure, corrosive conditions and mineral scaling inside devices, and seafloor machinery could be costly to repair. The systems will need expensive subsea cables to carry power to shore over potentially long distances. It’s a heavy lift.

Sources indicate that while the September sea trial didn’t go perfectly, Redd is happy with the results. The tech giant landed its 3-ton power plant on the seafloor near a natural vent and produced net energy from it — albeit for only 8.7 seconds. Technical difficulties and a power-cable failure cut the dive short.

According to recent reports, team members successfully operated the system remotely from Seattle through a fiber-optic network running along the seabed. Redd said he’s grateful for access to the network, which is part of the National Science Foundation’s Regional Cabled Array and operated by the University of Washington.

Endurance engineers also drilled what they called the world’s first subsea geothermal well at a site about 5,000 feet below the ocean’s surface. The 2-inch-wide, 52-foot-deep well delivered hydrothermal fluid, but the flow was too restricted to run the power plant, sending the team to the natural vent.

Redd noted there’s a lot of work ahead, but the team “made huge strides” in learning and in reducing the project’s risks.

Sources indicate that the tech giant now is developing Leopard, its 2-megawatt generator. After testing the technology at the research site off the Oregon coast, Endurance aims to deliver power from a Leopard system in Tonga next year as its first commercial project. Subsea geothermal energy could ultimately reduce the island nation’s reliance on imported diesel and put the startup one step closer to its objective of generating terawatts of planet-friendly energy.

“This was always the end goal,” Redd said. “Create something that is highly meaningful for the world.”.

Editor’s Note: Nate Bek of Ascend is a former GeekWire reporter.

  • According to recent reports, karpelès’ warning comes as Pump.fun has set a Nov.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Mt. Gox CEO Mark Karpelès has strongly warned users of Solana-based memecoin launchpad Pump.fun about potential major security risks associated with the fresh wallet migration process, which could put users' private keys at great risk.

According to recent reports, karpelès’ warning comes as Pump.fun has set a Nov. 30 deadline to stop allowing external wallet logins to its website. The platform is moving to email and social logins, which will enable users to access their accounts via Google, Apple and GitHub.

Industry observers note that but to maintain their current accounts, Pump.fun is asking users to import their private keys. This is what Karpelès thinks could compromise the security of their crypto assets.

In a recent X post, Karpelès stated he studied Pump.fun's JavaScript code to understand the nature of the new migration process.

The analysis has raised questions about the security of customers’ private keys, despite the platform's claims.

“At best, it's a misnomer to refer to it as 'end-to-end encryption,'” said Karpelès.

According to Karpelès, consumers' private keys are first encrypted in their browsers before being sent through Pump.fun’s servers to the platform’s wallet infrastructure provider, Privy.

Also, Pump.fun's backend provides the public key used for encryption during migration. Consumers’ browsers have no way to check whether the public key is authentic, according to Karpelès.

The possibility of a security breach involving Privy’s infrastructure is another major concern.

“Your money also now relies on Privy never getting hacked,” Karpelès warned.

One of the most crucial aspects of Karpelès' warning is the need for migration in the first place.

He stated Pump.fun could use signature-based authentication without forcing users to expose their private keys.

Pump.fun already uses a "Sign in with Solana" message to prove ownership of a wallet, according to Karpelès.

So theoretically, users can prove ownership of their wallets and execute transactions without having to import their private credentials into a new system.

#225330. 5 Kohl’s Black Friday offers, from dawn hours to a no-purchase $10,000 sweepstakes

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1405 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Qz ↗ Open Full Page

5 Kohl’s Black Friday offers, from dawn hours to a no-purchase $10,000 sweepstakes

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1405 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Qz

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • on Black Friday, 2026, with free Kohl’s Cash, Sephora coupons and a $10,000 sweepstakes.
  • Industry observers note that black Friday remains one of the biggest shopping days in the U.S., but much of that shopping now happens on phones and laptops rather than in store aisles.
  • Industry observers note that "So, retailers have to do more to entice people into stores and draw crowds," Saunders told TheStreet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kohl’s opens at 5 a.m. on Black Friday, 2026, with free Kohl’s Cash, Sephora coupons and a $10,000 sweepstakes. See what is worth the trip.

Industry observers note that black Friday remains one of the biggest shopping days in the U.S., but much of that shopping now happens on phones and laptops rather than in store aisles. TheStreet reports that Neil Saunders, managing director of retail at GlobalData, considers the day enormous but no longer the event it once was for shoppers. A retailer can't simply unlock its doors at dawn and count on a line outside. Stores now have to compete for the visit itself.

Industry observers note that "So, retailers have to do more to entice people into stores and draw crowds," Saunders told TheStreet. Kohl's $KSS faces that challenge partway through a recovery, and Michael Bender, Kohl's CEO, claims the company is not yet where it wants to be. Kohl's still has something to prove in its stores this weekend. The company has built its early hours and handouts to bring people into its stores, more than to mark the holiday.

Kohl's Black Friday plans include a dawn opening, Kohl's Cash envelopes, beauty coupons tied to its Sephora shops and a $10,000 sweepstakes, according to Mashable. Most of those offers reward a shopper for being inside a Kohl's at the right hour. That suits a manufacturer that wants people in its aisles rather than on its website. Some of the offers justify setting an early alarm, and others don't.

Industry observers note that kohl's $KSS is keeping its stores open from before sunrise until the last minute of Black Friday instead of relying on one rush at the door. Stores open at 5 a.m. on Friday, Nov. 27, and stay open until midnight local time, according to Mashable. With those hours, Kohl's can serve whoever comes in, whenever they come in, and doesn't have to reward only the shoppers who waited outside in the dark.

A 5 a.m. opening used to mark the moment the discounts began, but retailers now cut prices well before Black Friday. Kohl's is opening its doors to compete with sales that have been running for weeks and with shoppers who buy from home. For shoppers, 5 a.m. is when Kohl's unlocks its stores, not when the bargains start.

Recent findings suggest that for the reader, the generous part is the length of the day, not its early start. Someone who only wants Kohl's prices doesn't have to choose between a 5 a.m. alarm and skipping Black Friday entirely.

Kohl's $KSS keeps every one of its stores closed on Thanksgiving, Thursday, Nov. 26, and shoppers can reach its holiday deals only online that day, according to Mashable. On the holiday, Kohl's depends entirely on its website, the part of the business that has been shrinking. Online sales slipped 1% while comparable sales in its stores climbed 2%, according to TheStreet. That helps explain why its in-store offers cluster in the hours and days after Thanksgiving.

Kohl's closes on Thanksgiving as a standing rule, not as a one-off choice for this Black Friday. TheStreet reports that Kohl's also locks every store in the country on Easter Sunday and Christmas Day, under a holiday hours policy that covers three days a year. JCPenney and Macy's $M close their stores on Thanksgiving as well, so a department-store shopper who skips Kohl's that day finds neither rival open. The closure costs Kohl's no ground against those chains. Among them, the contest for in-person shoppers begins when they open their doors Friday morning.

Sources indicate that for a shopper, Thursday is a day to browse online and blueprint a list. The offers that reward showing up in person begin the next morning.

According to recent reports, kohl's $KSS will hand a Kohl's Cash voucher valued between $5 and $100 to each of the first 200 people inside every store once it opens at 5 a.m., according to Mashable. Kohl's ties the reward to showing up rather than to buying anything, and that is the kind of pull retail analyst Bruce Winder says stores now need. "Retailers need to offer an attractive incentive for shoppers to visit their store first," Winder told TheStreet. Kohl's sets the limit store by store, so a shopper's chances depend on the crowd at the local Kohl's, not on demand across the country. With the envelope, Kohl's is trying to turn an early opening into an actual crowd.

Kohl's is making a modest promise to a lot of people, and everyone near the front of the line goes home with something. Target $TGT is chasing the same early crowd with a similar offer. The first 100 guests at each Target store get a gift card worth $25, $50 or $100, and a single shopper at each store wins a $1,000 card, the largest amount Target is offering, according to TheStreet. The $100 is the top of the Kohl's range, not a likely result, and no breakdown of how the amounts are split has been given. The prize is store credit rather than money, so whatever it is worth gets spent at Kohl's.

Getting an envelope may take more effort than the offer suggests. Winder predicts that shoppers will wait a little longer in line on Black Friday, while the supply at each Kohl's stays fixed at 200 envelopes. Anyone who wants one should arrive well before the doors open, not right at 5 a.m. Saunders claims that a gimmick can succeed, though shoppers expect their time in a store to pay off. Nobody should make a predawn drive for a $5 voucher alone.

In a recent development, for shoppers who already had a Kohl's list, the envelope is a low-risk bonus. For everyone else, it is a lure, and Kohl's is counting on them to take it.

Kohl's $KSS is aiming its Saturday giveaway at a shopper it has not traditionally relied on. On Saturday, Nov. 28, each Kohl's store will hand a beauty coupon worth between $5 and $100 to the first 200 people through its doors, according to Mashable. Kohl's has long depended on older shoppers, according to CNBC, and the Sephora shops inside its stores are where the manufacturer looks for someone new. Blake Anderson, the analyst covering Kohl's at Jefferies, stated of those shops, "What's been a really interesting development for them is a creative use of their square feet and a way to try to drive not only sales, but new and younger customers.".

As with Friday's envelopes, there is no word on how the amounts are split among the 200 coupons. Shoppers receive the coupon instantly, so they can put it toward beauty products during the same visit. For someone who already restocks makeup or skin care at Sephora, an early Saturday line is a reasonable bet. For anyone else, it means giving up a morning for a prize of unknown size.

Sources indicate that kohl's is willing to hand out these coupons because it is planning for shoppers it hopes to keep for years, not just this weekend. CNBC reports that Bender sees the younger generation as the customers the tech giant can expand alongside in the years ahead.

The Saturday line will offer an early answer on whether a beauty discount can turn a one-time visitor into a regular.

Industry observers note that kohl's $KSS asks almost nothing of the people who enter its $10,000 sweepstakes. Entry is free, limited to one per U.S. adult and open from Friday, Nov. 27, through Monday, Nov. 30, with times set in Eastern Time, according to Mashable. Unlike the Friday envelopes and the Saturday coupons, the sweepstakes doesn't require beating a crowd. A shopper on the West Coast should still watch the clock near the end, because Kohl's sets the deadline by Eastern Time.

Industry observers note that kohl's has not stated how many people will win or how it will divide the prize, so the odds are impossible to judge. With entry free, the sensible move is to enter once and then forget about it.

It has been revealed that by keeping the sweepstakes open through Monday, Kohl's keeps its name in front of shoppers after the Friday cash and the Saturday coupons are gone. Kohl's opens this offer to more people than any other in the campaign, even if its value to any one entrant remains a guess.

Sources indicate that XRP's sharp price decline might have finally stopped, as the asset has started to form a trading range that could provide a foundation for a recovery going forward. The most likely support level here is $0.9, as the price has already tested it three times.

The rapid downfall of XRP began on November 5, essentially marking the beginning of a sharp decline for the asset. The failure to break above the 100 EMA effectively eliminated the possibility of an uptrend. The price failed to break the mid-term trend and declined rapidly.

Sources indicate that the declining trading volume is yet another signal. As the downtrend accelerated, investors reacted to the rapidly deteriorating market conditions by selling some of their holdings, further fueling the downward movement.

With the divergence of moving averages, volatility is decreasing, but a more established bearish trend is forming, unfortunately. The most likely outcome could be a deceleration of the trend and a halt to the current decline.

Recent findings suggest that fundamentally, the cryptocurrency market remains weak. Risk-on sentiment among investors has disappeared, while the crash in tech and AI stocks could further fuel outflows from Bitcoin and crypto. The recoveries we are witnessing right now remain largely speculative.

It is key to note that the $0.9 support level does not necessarily confirm that XRP has reached its bottom. The asset is still trading substantially below its major moving averages, with the 50 EMA and 100 EMA remaining out of reach for now.

Until XRP manages to reclaim at least the $1 psychological price level, any upward movement will most likely remain a short-term recovery rather than an actual trend reversal.

At the same time, the formation of a narrow trading range around $0.93 could give buyers some breathing room. If selling pressure continues to decrease and volume stabilizes, XRP might try recovering and taking a chance at breaking the $1-$1.05 price level, where the first serious resistance is most likely.

Wireless networking chip startup Altair nabs $100M investment

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (738 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Altair Semiconductor Ltd., a supplier of wireless networking chips for connected devices, today declared that it has raised $100 million in funding.
  • It has been revealed that maverick Silicon led the Series A round.
  • It has been revealed that connected devices such as wearables and industrial sensors transmit their data traffic via the same carrier infrastructure as smartphones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:38 EST / NOVEMBER 26 2026.

Altair Semiconductor Ltd., a supplier of wireless networking chips for connected devices, today declared that it has raised $100 million in funding.

It has been revealed that maverick Silicon led the Series A round. It was reportedly joined by Pitango, which invested $50 million in Altair when it spun out of Sony Corp. earlier this year. The Japanese electronics giant is said to have retained a stake.

It has been revealed that connected devices such as wearables and industrial sensors transmit their data traffic via the same carrier infrastructure as smartphones. However, they access that infrastructure in different ways. Connected devices using specialized, low-power network protocols to exchange data with each one and to upload readings to cloud-based backends.

According to recent reports, altair’s flagship modem chip, the ALT1550, supports several such protocols. The most advanced technology in the lineup is the 5G NR eRedCap protocol, which uses 5G networks to transmit data. It consumes significantly less power than a standard smartphone connection and can transmit up to 233 megabits per second.

It has been revealed that the ALT1550 also supports two alternative protocols called LTE-M and Cat 1bis. Both use 4G network infrastructure, which is more widely available than the latest 5G hardware. LTE-M can process up to 1 megabits per second, while Cat 1bis is ten times faster and uses more power.

The chip combines a transceiver that picks up and generates radio signals with a baseband processor. That’s a chip specifically optimized for wireless networking tasks. It’s supported by an onboard memory pool, power management circuits and a module that can connect to a satellite when there’s no cell tower nearby.

The ALT1550 is one of several chips offered by Altair. An earlier module, the ALT1255, supports a network protocol called NB-IoT that uses even less power than LTE-M and Cat 1bis. It’s designed for devices that only transmit data every few weeks or months. The ALT1255 provides additional power savings by deactivating many of its features when it’s not in use.

According to recent reports, altair says that its silicon can be found in millions of devices. Utilities use it to power smart meters, which automatically transmit usage data to the cloud and thereby remove the need for manual readings. Delivery companies can use Altair chips to track the location of their trucks. The tech giant’s modules also power medical devices, street lights and a wide range of other systems.

Altair will use its upcoming funding round to kick off the mass production of its flagship ALT1550 chip. Additionally, the tech giant aims to develop new networking products and grow its international presence.

#225327. So you got a Microsoft Voluntary Exit Offer? Here’s what to do next

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1388 w)
📖 Baca

So you got a Microsoft Voluntary Exit Offer? Here’s what to do next

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1388 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Nikesh Parekh on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:41 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:41 pm.
  • According to recent reports, nikesh (Niki) Parekh is a former Microsoft GM who is now CEO of Seattle-based AI talent recruiting startup Provn.
  • Tens of thousands of Microsoft employees have a big decision to make in the next few weeks: take the company’s offer to leave, or stay and take their chances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Nikesh Parekh on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:41 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:41 pm.

According to recent reports, nikesh (Niki) Parekh is a former Microsoft GM who is now CEO of Seattle-based AI talent recruiting startup Provn. This is the fourth post in his series on “Life after Big Tech,” including the Seattle startup guide, laid off at 50 and VC funding is changing dramatically.

Tens of thousands of Microsoft employees have a big decision to make in the next few weeks: take the company’s offer to leave, or stay and take their chances.

Microsoft chief people officer Amy Coleman declared the initiative in a memo on Oct. 26: a Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) for about 60,000 employees at level 70 and below, which includes general managers and some vice presidents, in the U.S., Canada, the U.K. and India. That’s roughly 27% of Microsoft’s 223,000 people. The firm expects 3,000 or fewer of them to accept.

Microsoft indicates the terms match its standard severance: base pay tied to level and tenure, continued stock vesting, a period of health coverage and career transition help. The severance package varies greatly based on the seniority or level of the employee and the number of years of service. Employees have until early December to decide and would leave by the end of the year.

According to recent reports, the offer follows the Voluntary Retirement Program (VRP) that Microsoft extended to about 8,750 U.S. employees in April. About 30% of them, or roughly 2,600 people, took that offer.

All of this comes as Microsoft cuts jobs and changes the kinds of roles it hires for, while pouring money into AI infrastructure and data centers. At the same time, AI is reshaping the broader workforce, flattening management layers and changing what employers look for in latest hires.

The worry I hear most is whether more layoffs are waiting on the other side. So the real choice is whether you leave on your own terms or let the tech giant decide for you.

I hear two questions from Microsoft employees thinking about the VEO: How easily can I get another job, and how hard is it to start a company right now?

Harder than you think, and it depends a lot on who you are. We are in the “low hire, low fire” economy.

In a recent development, there is MASSIVE demand for AI-native builders — product managers, data scientists and engineers — as companies adapt products to deal with AI. Companies are also in the process of adopting AI.

Recent findings suggest that one of the fastest-growing tech roles is the “Forward Deployed Engineer,” who implements AI solutions at customers. Security is also job #1 as models and agents get smarter and better at hacking legacy systems.

But it is very hard to be seen by recruiters and hiring managers right now. Candidates are using AI to customize their resumes to each job and using AI agents to apply, sending out 100 to 200 job applications per day. Recruiters are inundated with resumes and job applications, many of which are fake or inappropriate for the role.

It is critical to leverage your network in the job search, which can be hard if you have spent your entire career within one company.

Hiring managers have changed what they look for, too. AI fluency is becoming table stakes. The “process” of how you build/sell/market with AI is more key than what you build. Candidates are expected to show prototypes and proof of how they use AI tools every day.

The jobs themselves are changing. A friend told me last month that he wanted an engineering manager role. There are fewer manager roles in the market now.

It has been revealed that AI has driven a reduction in management layers and a general flattening of organizations. The engineering team at a small AI manufacturer today is a CTO and a group of strong individual contributors. It is normal for managers to have 10 to 30 direct reports now, versus five to 10 in the pre-AI era.

Product management, program management and design teams are shrinking, as well, as AI automates certain jobs.

Hiring managers may view spending your whole career at Microsoft as a yellow flag. Microsoft is an iconic but unusual company. Almost no one else sells to and services customers the way Microsoft does, with an account executive inside nearly every large enterprise in the world.

The skills that get you promoted in Redmond don’t always carry over to a 500- to 5,000-person software company.

It has never been easier to build a product, and it has rarely been harder to fund a manufacturer.

According to recent reports, software is cheap to build now. A product leader and an engineer using AI tools can ship in weeks what used to take a team a year.

Recent findings suggest that this cuts both ways for startups. Every good idea attracts a dozen competitors within months, and the big platforms will copy anything that works.

The true strength of a startup today is the ability to grow revenue swiftly and establish leadership in a beachhead market. The sales, marketing, product-led growth and distribution strategies are becoming the most critical parts of the business.

The bar for venture funding is extremely high. Jason Lemkin of SaaStr recently shared data from ICONIQ showing that top “AI forward” startups under $10 million in annual recurring revenue are growing 900% a year at the median.

Industry observers note that one venture investor told me they advise their portfolio companies that if they aren’t on track for a $10 million run rate within two years, they won’t raise another round. Last week I spoke with an investor who owns part of a business with $4 million in revenue, growing 100% a year and losing $1 million, and it can’t raise.

There are three fundraising paths.

1) Think VERY big, raise a lot and grow fast enough to justify it. Build an incredible team pursuing an ambitious idea. Raise a large round based on the promise of becoming the next Anthropic, OpenAI or legal AI startup Harvey. Many of the most interesting companies are not software or AI-related, but are “deep tech” companies in defense, robotics, energy and biotech.

2) Raise a moderate amount of money from angels, family offices and nontraditional funds to build a business that has the ability to be profitable on one round of financing. You can control your destiny by building a company that doesn’t rely on the venture capital funding market.

3) Bootstrap and build a business that you own. Fund it yourself, grow it with revenue and get to profitability.

The question that most people are NOT asking is: What do I really want?

Before December, block out an afternoon and think about the last time you were happy at work.

There are many frameworks for figuring out what you want in your career and life in general. I’m a fan of the Four Elements exercise. Write down three times in your career when you felt energized and effective. From those, work out what gives you energy, where you have the most impact, what culture you do best in and what your constraints are: money, kids, aging parents and how many more years you want to work.

On LinkedIn, I have seen examples of Microsoft employees taking the VEO to start their own businesses in property management, buy car washes, take time to recharge, spend time with family and travel.

Other employees are starting the job search in earnest but not taking the VEO. Many others are just getting back to work and doubling down on Microsoft.

Whichever way you go, start now. Start by aligning on your priorities and what you want from your career. If you stay, use the next year to build your skills with AI and to grow a network outside Redmond. If you leave to build something, decide early which of the three funding paths you’re on, because that choice shapes everything that follows.

The people I’ve watched land well after Substantial Tech had one thing in common: they knew what they wanted before they walked out the door, whether that was a fresh role, a firm of their own or a year with their family.

#225326. The referral source real estate agents overlook is sitting in the next office

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (802 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housingwire ↗ Open Full Page

The referral source real estate agents overlook is sitting in the next office

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (802 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that I’ve spent more than 25 years in this business, and one pattern has held strong in every market I’ve worked in: the agents who build lasting careers rarely do it alone.
  • It has been revealed that referrals between agents get less attention than they deserve.
  • Your brokerage is the most natural place to begin, and it’s often the most overlooked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I’ve spent more than 25 years in this business, and one pattern has held strong in every market I’ve worked in: the agents who build lasting careers rarely do it alone. They have a network of fellow agents who think of them first when a client needs help. At The Agency, we were built on that idea. We encourage our agents to reach across the aisle, even to competitors, because when agents collaborate, more deals get done and clients are better served.

It has been revealed that referrals between agents get less attention than they deserve. We talk constantly about our sphere of influence, past clients and social media. Yet a colleague who’s relocating a client to your market, or who’s overbooked and can’t take on a fresh listing, might hand you a deal worth far more than a month of lead generation. Those opportunities only come to agents who’ve earned a place in someone’s mind.

Your brokerage is the most natural place to begin, and it’s often the most overlooked. Most of us share an office, a leadership team and a set of tools with dozens or even hundreds of agents, and many of us barely know their names.

Introduce yourself. Show up at the sales meeting, the training and the broker open, and stay for the conversation afterward. Ask people what they specialize in, what kind of client they love working with, and what they’d happily hand off. You’ll learn who’s the go-to for condos, who knows the hillside neighborhoods best, and who’s the strongest negotiator in the building.

It has been revealed that that knowledge pays off promptly. When a client mentions a need outside your expertise, you’ll know exactly who to call. When a colleague gets a request that fits your strengths, they’ll know to call you. Trust inside a brokerage builds slowly, but once it’s there, it makes everyone’s business stronger.

Recent findings suggest that competition is part of this industry, and I won’t pretend otherwise. But the agent across the street at another firm is also a potential partner, and the best ones treat them that way.

Sources indicate that think about how much of real estate is geographic. Clients move across the country, across the state, sometimes across town into a different market. Your client in Los Angeles who’s buying in Aspen needs someone they can trust on the ground, and you can’t be that person. A thoughtful agent in Aspen, whom you’ve met and vetted, can. The same goes in reverse. That’s a referral built on mutual respect, and it often leads to repeat business flowing both ways for years.

Sources indicate that industry events, local board committees and MLS involvement are all excellent places to meet these people. You see how people handle disagreement, how they treat staff, and how they follow through. That’s the kind of insight no online profile will give you.

According to recent reports, if you want referrals, you have to be worth referring. When one agent sends a client to another, they’re putting their own reputation on the line. They want to know that their client will be taken care of, that communication will be prompt, and that the deal will be handled with integrity.

According to recent reports, so treat every interaction with another agent as an audition, whether or not it’s a referral situation. Return calls swiftly. Show up prepared. Be the person who makes a tough negotiation easier instead of harder. Agents remember who was gracious under pressure, and they remember who wasn’t.

Close the loop, too. If someone sends you a client, keep them updated and thank them, even when the deal takes months. It sounds small, but plenty of agents forget, and the ones who don’t stand out.

According to recent reports, I’d encourage agents to build  a simple structure around this. Set a goal to connect with a few new agents each month, one or two inside your brokerage and a few outside it. Grab coffee or hop on a quick call. Send a note when you see a colleague’s listing go under contract. Ask how you can be useful before you ask for anything.

In a recent development, it doesn’t take much time, just consistency and a willingness to see other agents as allies. Your next client might be working with an agent down the hall right now, or with one in a brokerage across the country. Sooner or later, that client will ask for a recommendation. Make sure the agent who gets asked already knows you.

Rainy Hake Austin is a brokerage leader at The Agency.

Elon Musk has reacted to a post by Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ), in which the latter shared that he used Grok Bot to tidy up his X following list.

According to CZ, the bot was tasked with removing inactive and abusive accounts from the list of people he follows, though accounts with constructive criticism were supposed to stay. CZ was not fully sure about the results, adding "AI did it" with a shrug emoji.

Musk replied with "Cool." Later, CZ added in the same thread that it "worked well so far.".

In a recent development, back in September, CZ had to address rumors about his account being hacked after customers noticed that he had unfollowed a number of profiles. Per CZ, at that time he removed accounts that were inactive for more than 30 days.

Since then, the product has received praise from Nvidia head Jensen Huang, who said in October that Grok Bot usage was "really skyrocketing." Musk himself claimed on SpaceX's Q3 earnings call that he had never seen a product grow this fast.

Recent findings suggest that on Coinbase, Grok was responsible for 59.54% of AI-agent trading volume from Sept. 14 to Sept. 21. For comparison, Claude had 13.37% and ChatGPT only 1.54%. Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong then named Grok the leading client for agentic traders on the platform, to which Musk also responded with "Cool.".

At the same time, there were complaints. NewCore researchers reported last week that Grok Bot made 31 unrequested access attempts to email, calendar, Slack and GitHub accounts on two employee laptops within five days, ignoring the command to stop.

It was only last month that Musk was trolling Binance after the exchange lost about $6.3 billion in a hack on Oct. 29, the largest one in crypto history so far. Among other things, Musk posted "Everyday is Zeroday" and replied with fire and laughing emojis to CZ's earlier warning about phishing links.

CZ then asked Musk to stop, calling it a "bad time to troll," and reminded him that Binance's $500 million investment in Twitter in 2022 has become a stake in SpaceX worth more than $1 billion.

Now, the two seem to be on good terms again.

Amazon threatens to leave NYC again, this time over delivery bill, as it rallies customers to fight it
