Small Business Saturday: 10 ways to shop local this Black Friday weekend

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4151 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Qz

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • These 10 ways to shop local on Small Business Saturday, from gift cards and independent bookstores to reviews and makers' markets, explain how each one helps a neighborhood business.
  • Sources indicate that where you buy a holiday gift decides how much of the money stays with the business that sold it.
  • According to recent reports, small Business Saturday sits right in the middle of that math.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

These 10 ways to shop local on Small Business Saturday, from gift cards and independent bookstores to reviews and makers' markets, explain how each one helps a neighborhood business.

Sources indicate that where you buy a holiday gift decides how much of the money stays with the business that sold it. A sale on a massive online marketplace comes with a commission the seller pays. A card payment comes with a processing fee the merchant absorbs. A gift card bought in November puts cash in a shop's register before the recipient ever walks through the door. None of that reveals up on a receipt, but all of it affects what an independent owner actually keeps.

According to recent reports, small Business Saturday sits right in the middle of that math. It falls on the Saturday after Thanksgiving, wedged between Black Friday and Cyber Monday. American Express $AXP started it in 2010 to carve out one day for independent businesses in a weekend that otherwise belongs to big-box chains and online deals. Independent shops, restaurants and service businesses now plan sales and events around it.

Sources indicate that for shoppers, the useful question is a practical one. Showing up matters, but some ways of spending leave more money with a local business than others. And several of the most helpful things you can do are free. A detailed review can help a shop turn up in map and search results. A word to a friend can bring in a customer the shop never had to pay to reach.

The 10 ideas below cover both kinds of support. Some involve buying: gift cards, books from an independent bookstore, orders placed through a shop's own website, food from local kitchens, classes given as gifts and finds from farmers markets and makers' markets. Others are about how you pay, what you post online and who you tell. One looks past the weekend altogether, since independent businesses depend on sales that keep coming through December and into the new year.

Industry observers note that each one works on its own. None takes a significant budget, and none guarantees a particular payoff for the business. Together, they're a handful of practical ways to point your holiday spending toward the shops, bookstores, bakeries and studios in your own neighborhood.

A gift card from an independent shop puts money in the owner's hands at the moment of sale. The merchandise stays on the shelf until the card is redeemed, and the recipient gets to choose what they want.

That timing matters for a small retailer. Holiday inventory is usually ordered and paid for well before December. Cash that comes in on Small Business Saturday helps cover those costs, even though the goods it pays for may leave the store long after the sale.

Gift cards also bring latest people through the door. A recipient who has never visited the shop now has a reason to walk in, browse and learn what it carries. Some recipients spend beyond the card's value. Others come back later on their own.

Most independent shops sell cards at the counter. Many also sell them through their own websites, often as digital cards delivered by email. A digital card suits a recipient who lives in another city or a gift that has to arrive on short notice. A physical card can go inside a holiday card or be wrapped with a small item from the same shop.

Read the terms before buying. In the U.S., the federal Credit CARD Act of 2009 bars most retail gift cards from expiring within five years. That clock runs from the purchase date or the last time money was loaded onto the card. State laws can add further protections. Ask whether the card works at every location if the business has more than one. Ask too whether it covers sale items, services or online orders.

Recent findings suggest that A small business can close or change hands. Keeping the receipt helps if a card is lost or disputed. Registering a digital card, where the shop offers that option, does the same.

The choice of shop can reflect the recipient. A card for a neighborhood hardware store, a toy shop or a record store points to their interests. It still leaves the final pick to them.

Sources indicate that an independent bookstore can get almost any book in print, not only the titles on its shelves. Booksellers routinely take special orders for titles a customer requests. Many also ship books to a customer's home or straight to a gift recipient.

Special orders run through the same channels a store uses to restock. Bookstores buy from publishers and from book wholesalers. Either route can usually supply a title that is still in print. Giving the bookseller the ISBN, the 13-digit number printed near the barcode, removes confusion between editions, translations and formats.

A special order usually takes longer than buying a book off the shelf. That makes holiday timing something to strategy around. Publishers' warehouses and shipping carriers handle heavy volume in late November and December. Popular titles can also sell out before a reprint arrives. Placing gift orders during Black Friday weekend leaves room for those delays.

Preorders follow the same logic for books not yet published. A shop can reserve a forthcoming title for a customer. It can then set the copy aside or ship it when the stock comes in.

Staff recommendations are one advantage of shopping in person. Booksellers spend their working days handling new releases and older backlist titles. Describing the recipient helps. A favorite author, a recent book they enjoyed or a subject they follow gives a bookseller enough to suggest titles a search algorithm might not surface. Many stores mark staff picks with handwritten shelf cards.

Sources indicate that check a shop's event calendar in December. Independent bookstores host author readings, signings, children's story hours and book club meetings. Some sell signed copies after those events. A signed book can make a more personal gift than a standard copy.

In a recent development, secondhand books are another option. Some independent shops sell used books alongside newly introduced ones. Dedicated used bookstores can carry out-of-print titles that a new-book shop has no way to order.

It has been revealed that ask about holiday services before checking out. Some shops offer gift wrapping. Others hold orders for in-store pickup or mail books to a recipient in another city.

Ordering from a local shop's own website, or calling the store, keeps the sale off large online marketplaces. Those platforms charge sellers a commission on each sale. A direct order leaves more of the purchase price with the business that made the sale.

Sources indicate that many independent retailers list products on big marketplaces to reach shoppers who would never find them otherwise. That reach comes at a cost. Marketplace sellers typically pay a cut of every order. Some platforms add charges for advertising, storage or fulfillment. The exact terms vary by platform and by product category.

According to recent reports, A shop's own site works differently. The merchant still pays for web hosting and an online store platform. No marketplace takes a share of each order, though. Shops that don't sell online at all can often take an order by phone or email instead.

In a recent development, finding the direct route is usually straightforward. A shop's web address often appears on its receipts, shopping bags, business cards and social media profiles. Searching the store's name along with its city can bring up the official site alongside any marketplace listings. When a product appears in both places, buying it on the shop's own site is the direct sale.

A shop's own site may also carry stock that never reaches a marketplace. One-off pieces, small batches and items made by nearby producers sometimes appear only there.

Industry observers note that check for local pickup before checkout. Many small retailers let customers order online and collect in store. That spares the buyer a shipping charge and spares the shop from preparing a parcel. It also brings the buyer through the door, where other items on the shelves are in view.

Recent findings suggest that shipping from a small shop can cost more or take longer than shipping from a large retailer with its own logistics network. Ordering early in the holiday season leaves room for that. Some shops post holiday shipping cutoff dates on their sites.

It has been revealed that direct orders also change who holds the customer relationship. Marketplaces often limit how sellers can contact buyers. When a shopper buys from the store's site, the shop can follow up on the order and answer questions itself. Returns and exchanges then go through the shop rather than a platform. Reading the store's own return policy before paying avoids confusion later.

Industry observers note that following an independent shop's stated payment preference is one of the simplest ways to help it on Small Business Saturday. A shop that asks for cash or debit is often trying to manage what card acceptance costs the business.

According to recent reports, every card sale carries processing fees. The merchant pays them, not the shopper. Several parties share those fees, including the bank that issued the card, the card network and the company that processes the payment. Depending on the processor, the charges come out of each deposit or arrive as a periodic bill.

Card money also takes time to arrive. Card sales settle through the processor and land in a merchant's bank account after a delay. Cash is in the register the moment the sale ends. For a small retailer paying for holiday inventory or covering extra staff in a busy month, that timing can matter.

In a recent development, preference is the operative word. Cash carries its own costs for a business. Someone has to count it, store it securely and take it to the bank. Some owners would rather skip that work and run a fully card-based or cashless counter. Paying cash at a shop that does not want it does not help the owner.

The clearest guide is the shop itself. Look for a sign at the register or a note on the shop's website. Some small businesses post a cash discount. Others add a surcharge for credit cards. Rules on surcharging vary by state and by card network. Card network rules generally bar surcharges on debit cards, even where credit surcharges are allowed.

Cashless stores are not allowed everywhere. Massachusetts, Latest Jersey, New York City, Philadelphia and San Francisco are among the places that generally require retail stores to accept cash. Those rules are meant to protect shoppers who do not have bank accounts or cards.

Industry observers note that A short question at checkout works when no sign is posted. Asking which payment method the shop prefers takes a few seconds. It costs the shopper nothing extra, and it leaves the decision with the owner.

Sources indicate that planning ahead makes this easier. Withdrawing cash before a trip to a downtown shopping district helps when several smaller vendors are on the list. Some pop-up sellers work mostly in cash, and a shopper without it may have to walk away from a purchase.

A specific, honest online review helps a local business appear when nearby shoppers search, and it costs the reviewer nothing. A review that names what was bought and how the visit went gives other customers far more to go on than a star rating alone.

It has been revealed that search engines and map apps treat reviews as one of several signals when deciding which nearby businesses to show. A shop with recent, detailed reviews gives those systems more information to work with. It also gives a stranger scrolling through results a concrete reason to walk in.

Sources indicate that the most useful reviews read like a short report. Name the product or service, such as a hand-thrown mug, a house-made hot sauce or a bike tune-up. Mention whether the item was in stock or ordered in, and how long the wait was. Describe what the staff did, whether that meant tracking down a size, wrapping a gift or suggesting an alternative. Those details answer the practical questions future customers tend to ask.

Timing shapes a review's value as well. A review posted soon after a Small Business Saturday visit captures details while they are fresh. A post that week adds a recent entry during a season when many shoppers are deciding where to spend. Photos of the storefront, the shelves or the purchase can add context that text cannot.

It has been revealed that honesty keeps a review useful. A balanced account that notes a long line or limited parking alongside good service gives readers a fuller picture than unqualified praise. Many review platforms bar reviews written in exchange for discounts or free products. A review should reflect a real purchase or visit. Owners can often reply publicly, and a constructive note gives them something concrete to act on.

Many independent shops work with limited advertising budgets. For a shop like that, its search listing and the reviews attached to it can be one of the first things a fresh customer sees. Each customer who writes a few clear sentences adds directly to that public record.

A short review takes only a few minutes. It can be written on a phone before leaving the parking lot or later that evening. It stays attached to the business listing long after the holiday weekend ends.

It has been revealed that farmers markets and holiday makers' markets let shoppers buy straight from the people who grow, cook or craft the goods on the table. With no wholesaler or retail middleman involved, the vendor sets the price and collects the sale directly, minus any stall fee the market charges.

It has been revealed that that direct link is the main difference from a store shelf. A farmer selling apples, winter squash or eggs at a market booth is often the same person who raised them. A potter, woodworker or soapmaker at a craft fair usually made the pieces on display and can explain how.

According to recent reports, holiday makers' markets tend to appear in late November and December. They are often held in school gyms, church halls, community centers, breweries and public squares. Many run for a single weekend or one evening. The window to shop them can be short.

Outdoor farmers markets also shift with the season. In colder parts of the U.S., some move indoors for winter and cut back to fewer market days. Others close until spring. A market's own website or social media page is usually the most reliable place to confirm dates, hours and location before going.

It has been revealed that shelf-stable goods make practical gifts from these markets. Honey, jams, maple syrup and dried herbs travel well and keep for weeks or longer. Candles, soap and ceramics hold up in shipping and storage. Fresh produce and baked goods are better suited to a host gift or a holiday meal.

It has been revealed that face-to-face buying also allows questions that a product listing rarely answers. Shoppers can ask what wood a cutting board is made of, how a glazed mug should be cleaned or whether a soap contains fragrance. Farmers can explain how a crop was grown and how to store it.

Many makers take commissions and custom orders, such as a personalized ornament or a piece in a specific color. These requests need lead time. Asking in late November or early December rather than the week before a holiday gives the maker room to finish the work.

Recent findings suggest that vendors at seasonal markets often have no permanent storefront. Picking up a business card or noting a maker's name makes it possible to find them again. Many also sell between markets by email, by phone or at other recurring events.

It has been revealed that A local class or service works as a holiday gift that sends money to a nearby business owner instead of a distant warehouse. A pottery class, a haircut or a pass for a neighborhood fitness studio all fit this approach.

Service businesses sell time and skill rather than stocked inventory. That puts studios, salons and independent instructors outside the doorbuster discounts that dominate Black Friday weekend promotions. A gift of their time gives them a holiday sale that doesn't depend on a shelf of products.

According to recent reports, most of these businesses sell gifts in one of a few forms. A studio may offer a single-session certificate, a multi-class pack or a set membership period. Salons and barbershops often sell certificates for a named service, such as a cut or a color appointment. Some instructors sell seats in a specific workshop on a set date. A question at the front desk will show which formats a business offers.

In a recent development, booking terms matter more for experiences than for physical goods. Classes fill up, and instructors keep limited schedules. Some sessions run only in certain months. Before buying, check whether the gift is tied to a date and how far ahead the recipient needs to book. Ask what happens if they need to reschedule. Expiration rules vary by business and by location. Confirm them at the time of purchase.

Sources indicate that A gift that fits the recipient's interests is easier for them to use. A beginner wheel-throwing class suits someone who likes working with their hands. A cooking class can suit someone who hosts often. A massage, a tailoring appointment or a bike tune-up can suit someone who rarely books those services for themselves.

It has been revealed that many of these businesses work in small groups or one-on-one sessions. That format gives the recipient direct time with an instructor, stylist or technician. It also introduces the recipient to a business they may return to on their own.

Industry observers note that A gift for two is another option. Paired classes, such as a couples' cooking night or a two-person workshop, let the giver attend alongside the recipient. Some studios also sell private group sessions for families or friends. Those sessions can double as a shared holiday outing.

The same idea works for a recipient who lives in another city. Many studios and salons take gift orders by phone or online. A giver can buy a session at an independent business near the recipient's home rather than near their own.

Ordering pies, platters and party trays from a neighborhood bakery or restaurant moves holiday food spending to local kitchens. Order early, order directly and blueprint the pickup. Many small kitchens can only produce so much in a single week.

According to recent reports, catering follows a similar timeline. Restaurants that sell trays of appetizers, roasted meats or side dishes usually ask for a headcount and a pickup date in advance. Some ask for a deposit to hold the order. Calling with a rough guest count makes it easier for the kitchen to suggest portions and quantities.

Dietary questions are easier to sort out with a local kitchen than with a packaged product. Customers can ask what goes into a dish and how it is prepared. They can also ask whether it contains nuts, dairy or gluten. Some small bakeries make egg-free or dairy-free versions on request. Shared equipment can still mean cross-contact. Asking the kitchen directly is the reliable way to know.

It has been revealed that how an order is placed also matters. Calling the restaurant, ordering at the counter or using its own online ordering page keeps the sale off third-party delivery apps. A direct order also lets staff confirm details or flag a sold-out item before the event.

Pickup is the final step. Holiday pickup days tend to be crowded, and many shops assign time slots to keep lines moving. Arriving within the assigned window helps the kitchen hand off orders while the food is fresh. Asking for reheating instructions for hot dishes saves guesswork at home.

The same approach works for more than one dinner. Office parties, Upcoming Year's gatherings and winter potlucks all call for platters, desserts and bread. Restaurants that do not advertise catering may still take a large takeout order if a customer asks a few days ahead.

In a recent development, small Business Saturday lasts a single day, but local shops need customers for the rest of the holiday season and well into the fresh year. Spreading purchases across December and January gives independent businesses steadier sales than one busy weekend can.

The Saturday event puts independent retailers in the spotlight for one weekend. The weeks that follow still bring gift buying, holiday hosting and year-end errands.

Industry observers note that last-minute gifts are easier to find at a store close to home. National carriers publish holiday shipping cutoffs, and orders placed after those dates may not arrive before Christmas. A shop down the street already has its stock on the shelf. A shopper can walk in on Dec. 23 and leave with a gift in hand.

Industry observers note that local staff can also help with a late gift. They know what is in stock and can suggest an alternative when a planned item has sold out. Some independent shops also wrap gifts at the counter. That saves time in the final days before a holiday.

January brings its own reasons to buy close to home. Exchanges and returns are simpler when the store is nearby and the owner can handle them in person. Post-holiday clearance sales help local shops move seasonal inventory. Cold-weather needs such as boots, coats, snow shovels and ice melt send people to hardware and clothing stores in many parts of the U.S.

Industry observers note that the quieter stretch after the holidays matters for owners too. Foot traffic often drops once the gift season ends. Rent, payroll and utility bills keep arriving each month regardless. A purchase during a slow week adds revenue when fewer customers are coming through the door.

Industry observers note that one version of this approach is a routine. Picking up coffee beans, a birthday card or a replacement hardware part from an independent shop turns occasional support into regular business. Those everyday errands happen in every month, not only in late November.

Sources indicate that one practical rule is to check a local store before ordering something online. That habit carries the purpose of Small Business Saturday into the rest of the year.

In a recent development, telling friends about a local shop, or sharing its posts online, points new customers toward an independent business at no cost to you. The recommendation comes from someone the listener already knows, which gives it weight with them.

Independent shops rarely have the marketing budgets of national chains. At many of them, the owner or a single employee runs the shop's social media accounts alongside other work. Each share, tag or mention carries the shop's name to people outside its usual audience.

According to recent reports, specific recommendations give friends something to act on. Saying a shop "is great" offers little detail. Naming the hand-poured candles, the cheese counter or the employee who tracked down a hard-to-find gift tells a friend why to go. It also tells them what to ask for.

According to recent reports, social media makes this kind of referral easy to repeat. Posting a photo of a holiday purchase and tagging the shop's account lets followers click straight through to its profile. Resharing the shop's own posts spreads the details an owner most wants customers to see. Those posts often cover new stock, extended holiday hours or a Small Business Saturday event.

Recent findings suggest that adding a location tag to a post connects it to the shop's address. That helps followers who live nearby figure out where to find it.

In a recent development, private messages and group chats count, too. A friend stuck on a gift for a relative can get a quick text with a link to a shop that fits. That one message can send a customer the shop might not have reached otherwise.

It has been revealed that email newsletters offer another direct line. Signing up means hearing about sales, restocks and events straight from the shop. The news arrives without depending on what a social platform chooses to display. Forwarding a newsletter to a friend passes that information along.

Neighborhood groups and community forums are another outlet. Someone may ask for gift ideas or a place to find a particular item. Naming a local shop in reply puts it in front of a person already planning to buy.

Some owners prefer that customers not photograph certain items, displays or staff. Asking before posting from inside a shop respects that preference.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The United States Department of Justice (DOJ) has initiated a significant legal push to address the theft of over $6 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance by North Korean hackers last month.

As per a Nov. 23 announcement, the DOJ mentioned that it has filed a civil forfeiture complaint to recover over $1.1 billion worth of stolen cryptocurrency as part of its efforts to retrieve the billions lost in the massive hack.

In a recent development, the recent development comes less than a month after North Korean hackers reportedly broke into Binance on Oct. 29 in one of the biggest crypto heists ever.

In a recent development, the DOJ claimed that its recent civil forfeiture action focuses on over $1.1 billion worth of USD Coin (USDC), a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar and issued by Circle.

The assets are alleged to have been stolen from Binance and laundered by North Korean cybercriminals.

Significantly, the assets had previously been frozen under a restraining order obtained by the government earlier this month. With the fresh court filing, the potential recovery of the assets has taken another step forward.

According to recent reports, the DOJ further claimed that U.S. authorities have successfully helped freeze, seize or return over $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency since the attack in October.

This is nearly half of the total $6 billion-plus stolen from Binance, though the government did not provide details about how much of that has been returned to the exchange.

Sources indicate that the importance of collaboration between law enforcement agencies and crypto firms to ensure that hackers don't get away with stolen assets was stressed by Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva.

“North Korean cyber hackers stole over $6 billion of cryptocurrency from Binance. But prompt coordination with both the government and our private sector partners helped to avoid the bulk of these assets from being lost,” Duva said.

U.S. authorities have further revealed the sophisticated money laundering techniques used by North Korean hackers to conceal their stolen cryptocurrency.

FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman remarked that the regime uses intricate money laundering methods to convert stolen digital assets into funds for its illicit activities.

After the Binance hack, authorities quickly worked to trace the stolen funds and coordinate with crypto service providers to block further transfers.

The U.S. Secret Service claimed that its investigators were able to detect and freeze some of the stolen funds within minutes of the hack.

"The bad actors in this intrusion thought they could run from law enforcement. They've found out they were wrong," stated Secret Service Special Agent in Charge Todd Bratz.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 23, 2026 at 8:25 amNovember 23, 2026 at 8:27 am.
  • Amazon confirmed Monday morning that it will acquire Decart’s AI optimization technology, known as the Decart Optimization Stack, and bring on the 3-year-old startup’s founders and team of AI researchers and engineers.
  • It has been revealed that amazon didn’t disclose financial terms.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 23, 2026 at 8:25 amNovember 23, 2026 at 8:27 am.

Amazon confirmed Monday morning that it will acquire Decart’s AI optimization technology, known as the Decart Optimization Stack, and bring on the 3-year-old startup’s founders and team of AI researchers and engineers.

It has been revealed that amazon didn’t disclose financial terms. Amazon agreed to pay about $7.5 billion for the assets, Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the matter. The deal is tied to performance targets over five years, Globes reported.

The deal could boost Amazon’s push to compete with Nvidia, which sells most of the chips used for training and running AI models today. Amazon makes its own AI chips, called Trainium, and has signaled plans to start selling them directly to other companies, beyond its own AWS data centers.

“We believe we’re going to have a very significant business selling chips externally,” CEO Andy Jassy noted on the company’s earnings call last month.

Amazon unveiled the deal the same day Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, ending a leadership shakeup at the chipmaker that put CFO Colette Kress in the interim role.

According to recent reports, decart’s software is designed to get more performance out of each chip, one of the main selling points Amazon needs to win those external customers. Microsoft is building its own Maia chips, mainly for its own AI services, and Google has its TPUs.

In a recent development, decart’s software has also run on chips from Nvidia and Google. Amazon didn’t say whether that will continue.

“Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip,” noted Peter DeSantis, Amazon’s senior vice president of foundational AI models, custom silicon and quantum computing, in the blog post announcing the acquisition.

Sources indicate that decart’s three co-founders are joining Amazon: CEO Dean Leitersdorf, his brother Orian Leitersdorf and Moshe Shalev. Amazon isn’t buying Decart’s AI models, Bloomberg reported. Those include Lucy, which edits live video in real time, and Oasis, which generates interactive virtual worlds.

Sources indicate that the deal runs through Annapurna Labs, Amazon’s chip unit, and Decart’s technology will be used to improve performance on Amazon’s Trainium and Inferentia AI chips, according to Globes. The Israeli business publication reported that Annapurna co-founder Nafea Bshara led the negotiations for Amazon.

The founders, who own about 64% of Decart, have committed to stay at Amazon for five years and could receive about $4.8 billion collectively, Globes reported.

Amazon bought Annapurna, also founded in Israel, in 2015 for a reported $350 million. Its engineers went on to design Trainium and Amazon’s other custom chips.

Amazon and Decart have worked together since 2025. Decart was among the first customers on Trainium3, and Amazon remarked last December that Decart was running real-time video four times faster on Trainium at half the cost of GPUs.

Industry observers note that the deal follows Amazon’s release last month of TorchNeuron, a tool that runs common AI code on Trainium with minimal changes. Both moves target the software advantage that has kept developers on Nvidia hardware, as GeekWire explained when the talks surfaced in October.

Decart drew interest from other major buyers before Amazon. Anthropic was in talks to acquire it for about $6 billion, Bloomberg reported in August, before it walked away in September. Nvidia held earlier acquisition talks, according to CTech, and invested in Decart’s $300 million funding round in May.

“From day one, our mission has been to redefine the boundaries of what AI can do and to make it dramatically more efficient along the way,” Dean Leitersdorf noted in Amazon’s announcement. “Joining Amazon gives our team the scale, the customers, and the infrastructure to pursue that mission faster than we could on our own.”.

Industry observers note that the deal is subject to regulatory clearance. Amazon didn’t say what happens to Decart’s AI models or to its existing customers, such as eBay, which is also an investor in the startup.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The chief executive of one of the world’s leading fashion brands has stated that the intense and often slow process of craftswomen and men making products by hand has become a vital skill in a world of online “instant gratification.”.

Leena Nair, the CEO of Chanel, said that business leaders are living through an “unprecedented” period of transformation and fragility, adding that it was time to prioritize human ingenuity and talent.

“Macro-economic shifts, huge leaps in AI and technology and geopolitical instability, these are challenges affecting all sectors,” she told the annual gala dinner of the French Chamber of Great Britain, which brings together U.K. and French business executives, policy makers, and cultural leaders.

“And in this context of disruption, the power of creation and beauty has never been more vital or more precious. Creation and beauty have been vital sources of inspiration and joy for thousands of years. They’re even more precious today in a world of constant instant gratification, constant overstimulation, and infinite touch points.”.

Nair, who has been Chanel CEO since 2022, saw the luxury brand return to growth last year, led by an increase in sales in America. Global revenues rose by 1.8% compared with 2024 to $19.3 billion, while operating profits rose 5.2% to $4.7 billion.

Nair stated there was a growing body of scientific evidence that revealed that exposure to art and human-led creative work led to higher levels of happiness and performance.

“This growing body of academic research indicates how encounters with beauty correlate directly to a greater sense of human flourishing at work and in life,” she mentioned. “In recent years, we see growing scientific evidence of the improving impact that arts and culture has on physical and mental well-being.”.

“In this context of disruption, the power of creation and beauty has never been more vital or more precious”.

Over 95% of Chanel’s customers are women, Nair noted, adding that “beauty” is a very notable driver of how people respond to the world around them. She said that one customer who had been through surgery said that buying crafted products was part of her recovery.

“Surgeons tell me this all the time, that when surgery is over they know the women are back to normal when they ask to put on their makeup for the first time,” she noted.

Sources indicate that many leaders of luxury brands often feel ignored when it comes to policy debates about economic growth. In the U.K., the end of foreign visitors being able to shop without incurring the national sales tax has caused controversy. In the U.S., new tariffs targeting luxury goods have unsettled markets.

“Luxury is an economic powerhouse, it’s a cultural powerhouse and an emotional powerhouse,” Nair remarked. “To put that scale into context, European high-end luxury brands generate a trillion dollars in business every year. That’s 5% of Europe’s GDP. “It’s not a niche sector. More than 2 million people work in the sector across Europe.”.

Chanel works with the King’s Foundation, King Charles III’s organization that supports the retention and development of traditional skills.

“It looks simple, but to do a pleated skirt takes eight hours of pushing a cardboard mold back and forth by two talented artisans doing it the right way,” Nair stated, arguing that Chanel continues to invest in “skills that will otherwise be lost, working with extraordinary artisans and partners, many of whom we have worked with for generations.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • On the same migration page, a block of instructions written for AI coding assistants still says Noble, Sui and Aptos "still require V1." Circle's own release notes say two of those three chains moved to V2 weeks ago.
  • Circle's legacy cross-chain transfer protocol entered its final month today.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Burn limits on Circle's legacy USDC bridge began falling on October 31, and the V1 contracts pause on December 1.

On the same migration page, a block of instructions written for AI coding assistants still says Noble, Sui and Aptos "still require V1." Circle's own release notes say two of those three chains moved to V2 weeks ago.

Circle's legacy cross-chain transfer protocol entered its final month today. From October 31, burn limits on CCTP V1 start falling toward zero, and on December 1 the V1 contracts pause. Any app still using them will stop moving USDC between chains.

Most coverage has focused on those two dates. But the guide developers are told to follow, Circle's V1-to-V2 migration page, contains a mistake in the section written for AI tools.

According to recent reports, embedded in the page is an "Agent Instructions" block, guidance meant for AI coding assistants that read the documentation for developers. It claims: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1." For two of those three chains, Circle's other published records say the opposite.

The schedule is fixed. Circle unveiled in an August 27 blog post that "CCTP V1 (Legacy) deprecation begins October 31, 2026 and completes on December 1, 2026.".

From today, V1 burn limits fall, and the migration guide claims "message limits will tighten over time until no new burns can be initiated." On December 1 the V1 contracts pause, and any integration still pointing at them can no longer transfer USDC between chains.

Recent findings suggest that circle has been firm about this. "Migration from CCTP V1 (Legacy) to CCTP V2 is required, not just recommended," the manufacturer wrote, adding that V2 "uses separate contracts and APIs and is not backward compatible.".

Recent findings suggest that funds already in transit are protected. The guide says "all pending redemptions will remain available" during the phase-out, and that Circle "will maintain minter allowances greater than the total of pending attestations.".

Industry observers note that the migration page has two audiences. Human readers see the main guide. AI coding assistants also parse a separate instruction block, which tells them how to answer developer questions.

In that block, the guidance is clear: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1.".

The main text above it says something different. According to the human-facing guide, "CCTP V2 contracts are available on all CCTP V1 chains except for Noble and Sui," and "Sui will be supported by V2 before the deprecation begins." Aptos isn't listed as an exception there at all.

So one page gives two different answers about the same chains, and the out-of-date answer is the one written for AI tools.

Circle's 2026 CCTP release notes show how out of date the instruction is:.

It has been revealed that circle's supported chains and domains page now lists both Sui and Aptos in its CCTP table, with Standard Transfer support. The page's V1-only section names one chain: Noble.

Sources indicate that as of today, Aptos has had V2 for more than two months and Sui for more than three weeks. The instruction telling AI tools that both "still require V1" was overtaken by Circle's own updates before the shutdown began.

Noble is the one chain in that line where the instruction is still accurate, and it is leaving CCTP entirely.

In a September 10 announcement, Circle remarked "Noble will not receive CCTP V2" and set out its exit:.

For Noble, V1 is the only route available, and it is being closed.

A wrong line in documentation would normally be a small issue, but the timing makes this one more serious.

Many developers now ask AI assistants to write or update integration code, and those assistants read documentation like this page. A developer asking how to bridge USDC to Sui or Aptos could be told, based on Circle's own instruction block, to use V1. That is the route whose burn limits started falling today and which pauses in a month.

Recent findings suggest that the fix in the code is not small either. Moving to V2 means:.

An integration built on V1 now would have to be rebuilt within weeks.

For teams working with Sui and Aptos, the published records point one way: build on V2, using the contract addresses for domains 8 and 9. Don't follow the V1 guidance from the agent-instruction block.

For Noble, the deadline is January 12, 2027. Before then, integrators need to remove Noble as a CCTP route, and holders need to move or redeem their USDC.

It has been revealed that for everyone else, the burn-limit reductions have started. December 1 is the last day V1 integrations work, and any app still on V1 after that will stop moving USDC between chains.

As the workday progresses, you face small problems. Your phone is almost dead, with no charger in sight. You can’t find the piece of paper with yesterday’s meeting notes.

None of these small issues necessitates a complete office makeover. Sometimes you just need a small upgrade to make life easier, like a charging station for your devices, a lamp that puts light where you need it or a voice recorder that transcribes meetings for you.

Black Friday is one of the best times to shop for office technology. The right purchase can remove everyday irritations — or simply make your workspace more pleasant — at a discounted price.

The list price for the charging station is $80, but it is 41% off for Black Friday, bringing the price down to $47.

Breaking: Swiss Bitcoin ETF: Bitcoin Wasn’t the Problem, Institutional Rules Were – BIT CEO

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahmed Barakat is a journalist and copywriter based in Georgia with a growing focus on blockchain technology, DeFi, AI, privacy, digital assets, and fintech innovation.

In a recent development, the CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Sources indicate that europe’s first spot Bitcoin ETF launched with 350 BTC worth more than $20 million, opening a new chapter for the country’s regulated crypto investment market. BIT Asset Management’s Bitcoin Fund ETF (BBIT) began trading on the SIX Swiss Exchange yesterday with Bitcoin exposure through a Swiss fund structure.

BBIT itself carries an annual expense ratio of 0.19% and is at the moment Europe’s only active spot Bitcoin ETF.

According to recent reports, 🇨🇭 Today, Bitcoin Fund ETF (BBIT) will list on SIX Swiss Exchange: Switzerland’s first and only FINMA-approved Bitcoin ETF.🕘 Trading opens at 9:00 CET (8:00 UTC)News announcement: https://t.co/N112jUZiUP*Switzerland only. Not for US persons. Capital at risk. pic.twitter.com/CJa7lkh3uT.

According to recent reports, the launch followed an 18-month regulatory process, with FINMA approving the fund on October 20. The approval then allows BBIT to invest exclusively in Bitcoin under a specific exemption from diversification requirements, opening a route for investors whose mandates restrict them to fund-based investments.

“Some institutional investors may face internal investment restrictions that permit investments only through fund structures,” Dominik Oggenfuss, CEO of BIT Asset Management, told Cryptonews in an exclusive comment.

Switzerland already has an established market for Bitcoin investment products, but not every investor can use every available vehicle. Some institutional mandates permit investments in funds while restricting exchange-traded notes or other product structures, creating a compliance barrier even when Bitcoin exposure is otherwise allowed.

In a recent development, BBIT addresses these differences through its Swiss fund structure, operating under Swiss fund law and FINMA oversight. Rather than relying on futures contracts or gaining Bitcoin exposure through an issuer’s debt, BBIT fund holds Bitcoin directly.

In a recent development, its holdings are stored in cold storage through AMINA Bank under Swiss banking regulation, offering institutions a custody arrangement within Switzerland’s financial system. Investors can buy fund shares through participating banks and brokers on SIX, using existing investment infrastructure, bypassing the hassles of managing wallets or/and private keys.

Oggenfuss remarked the fund was designed for investors who already had Bitcoin exposure but wanted a different regulatory and custody arrangement.

“Some investors already had access to Bitcoin through ETPs but would prefer a Swiss fund structure under Swiss Fund Law, regulated by FINMA, combined with a Swiss cold-storage solution provided by AMINA Bank under Swiss banking regulation,” he said.

Industry observers note that this structure could make a difference for institutions operating under strict investment policies. These restrictions dictate eligible asset classes, legal structures, custody arrangements and counterparties, so a new investment vehicle can open access even when the underlying asset is already available elsewhere.

BBIT also offers Bitcoin-in-kind subscriptions, allowing eligible investors to contribute Bitcoin directly to the fund. Combined with its 0.19% expense ratio, the fund is positioning itself at the center of institutional infrastructure, cost, and operational convenience.

In a recent development, “BIT Group is not a firm that discovered Bitcoin recently. From one of the first Satoshi White Paper translations to a Swiss Bitcoin ETF, that continuity is a story many competitors cannot tell,” Oggenfuss said.

Recent findings suggest that BIT is presenting BBIT as the culmination of a much longer involvement with Bitcoin. Switzerland’s exchange market has been building crypto investment infrastructure for nearly a decade. SIX introduced Bitcoin-linked structured products in 2016, followed by physically backed crypto investment products as the market expanded.

The growth of these products has expanded access to Bitcoin through regulated exchanges, but fund mandates continued to dictate which structures institutions could use. BBIT introduces another option within this existing ecosystem, placing direct Bitcoin holdings inside a Swiss fund framework.

BBIT’s 350 Bitcoin launch gives the ETF a starting base of more than $20 million as BIT looks to attract investors through Swiss banking and brokerage networks. Now, we will see if this can turn regulatory approval and structural flexibility into sustained inflows.

With the deeper correction in the cryptocurrency market, we are finally witnessing somewhat of a bounce in multiple top-15 digital assets, including XRP, Monero and Dogecoin.

XRP is printing higher network usage compared to October, Monero is gradually outperforming the market in the last 24 hours and Dogecoin is aiming at a local price recovery, even though a modest one.

It has been revealed that one important development that we haven't anticipated is Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia (NVDA) CEO on November 23, only 11 days after his resignation. The announcement triggered a substantial market retrace, with NVDA stock gaining over 30% and Nasdaq adding around 6.8%, recovering a large share of last week's losses.

Recent findings suggest that thankfully, XRP shows us resilience beyond regular market metrics: the average daily payments throughout the month have crossed the 1.1 million threshold, a 107% growth versus the October baseline. The basis behind the reversal is considerable: the rise in market volatility that triggered a substantial breakdown in the asset.

With rapid market swings, it's no surprise that the asset saw more than 1.33 million transactions throughout the first 7 days of the month. New accounts over a rolling 24-hour period reached 4,065 wallets, per XRPScan query on November 23.

According to recent reports, from the technical standpoint, XRP is currently trading near the $0.99 price level, approximately 23% lower compared to the 30-day average, which fits the aforementioned bearish narrative. The decline in spot trading volume is also an important sign: spot investors dropped around 22.5% of their trading activities throughout the month.

The drop in futures volume also makes the picture slightly more complicated than it should be. Following the price breakdown, the volatility increase was followed by an increase in open interest, so the drop we're witnessing right now is more of a return to the baseline than an problem on its own.

The current price resistance and support points are quite diverse, but not thoroughly tested, apart from a local support level at $0.9. The immediate breakout test is going to take place at approximately $0.99, with a possibility of a further recovery. The level at $1.00 is more of a psychological barrier, while $1.04 is the threshold that should mark the end of the downtrend.

According to CoinMarketCap's data, Monero has been steadily underperforming XRP and Dogecoin in the last 24 hours, though it's important to separate rising demand and active speculative buying. In the last 24 hours, Monero has gained over 4.7% in price. Futures open interest has crossed the $230 million mark.

In a recent development, as already mentioned, Monero is a weaker performer out of the three, with a 4.7% gain over the last 24 hours. Unexpectedly, a deeper look reveals a set of issues: spot and futures volume, open interest and liquidation volume suggest a rather stale market with no momentum rather than an explosive recovery that might turn into a proper uptrend. The good news is that most of the liquidated volume is on the short side.

From the network usage perspective, Monero is struggling, with its transaction count dropping below the 30-day average, prompting baseless price resilience. Though Monero's network design certainly limits the possibility of a thorough analysis due to its protected transaction design.

Recent findings suggest that the most important development around Monero was, of course, the most recent Wrapped Monero incident. Despite the wrapped token itself having little to do with the main network of the asset, the coin itself had to withstand the rippling selling pressure. The token lost more than 99% of its value, causing $13 million in losses.

The main network itself went through a security audit on November 18, which found no high- or medium-severity vulnerabilities and only minor security issues, which developers have been notified about.

If the technical side of the question is rather key, the most important immediate price levels are the 508-510 range, which corresponds to the current breakout area, and the immediate support at $500.

Compared to all three cryptocurrencies, Monero is the only one showing some positivity over the last 7 days, despite the wrapped token incident. Privacy assets like XMR or Zcash quite often provide more market resilience during breakdowns, most likely due to the demand for privacy that always exists in the industry.

Dogecoin's technical recovery attempt is hitting somewhat of a wall, with daily, weekly and four-hour trends showing a clear bearish dynamic in addition to the price moving below all 8 tracked moving averages on the chart.

Industry observers note that as the CoinGlass data suggests, the trading activity we are witnessing today is mixed: spot and futures volumes are descending, with a slight increase in open interest. $584 million in futures volume and $86 million in spot volume. Long and short liquidations are balanced.

It has been revealed that unfortunately, the lack of network activity suggests a baseless price recovery on the market right now: only 37 thousand addresses were active in the last 24 hours, a 24% decrease YTD. Additionally, explorer data suggests that the ten largest DOGE addresses hold more than 44% of the token's available supply.

It doesn't suggest that only 10 customers hold a large part of the token's supply, but rather a high concentration of DOGE on exchanges, which quite often prompts additional selling pressure.

Industry observers note that with the low volume and open interest, any technical price level, both resistance and support, can get invalidated swiftly; however, highlighting them could be useful. The first resistance rests at $0.0599, with a trend recovery threshold located around $0.06.

Support levels lie all the way down to the important psychological level of $0.05, the nearest being $0.054. The obvious trend reversal threshold is, of course, $0.06. Until the price establishes a foothold above it, discussing a recovery is not the best option out there.

#225250. 5 trends that will define 2027—and how to invest in them

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1923 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fortune ↗ Open Full Page

5 trends that will define 2027—and how to invest in them

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1923 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fortune

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Heraclitus, the Greek philosopher, is often credited with the idea that the only constant in life is change.
  • In 2024, it appeared that pandemic-era inflation had been tamed, and the Federal Reserve responded with a series of cuts to its benchmark interest rate.
  • Industry observers note that this is glum news for homebuyers and the real estate industry, and for sectors including AI, which count on cheap credit to keep their businesses humming.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Heraclitus, the Greek philosopher, is often credited with the idea that the only constant in life is change. He was writing around 500 BC, but he could just as easily have been describing 2027, a year poised to bring seismic shifts in politics, technology, markets, and the way we live and work. Some of what’s coming is already in plain sight, like the AI revolution. Other forces are quieter but could prove just as consequential, including a likely surge in solar construction. Here are the five trends Fortune believes will define the coming year, and how investors can position themselves for each.

In 2024, it appeared that pandemic-era inflation had been tamed, and the Federal Reserve responded with a series of cuts to its benchmark interest rate. This optimism didn’t last, however, and price shocks from tariffs and the Iran war led the Fed to boost rates in 2026. The central bank is expected to continue on this path.

Industry observers note that this is glum news for homebuyers and the real estate industry, and for sectors including AI, which count on cheap credit to keep their businesses humming. But high interest rates are not bad for everyone. Beneficiaries include individual savers, who can look forward to higher income, and big banks whose business involves lending money.

While banks tend to earn more from loans when rates are higher, it is the “goliath” banks that do best in these environments, noted Mike Mayo, head of U.S. large-cap bank research at Wells Fargo Securities. For 2027, Mayo said JPMorgan Chase (JPM) and Bank of America (BAC), in particular, appear poised for a strong year based on bullish guidance they have issued. But he cautions that high interest rates only act as a tailwind up to a point—and that a rapid series of hikes would put larger portions of the economy under strain, counteracting the positive effect of higher interest rates for banks.

Mayo dismissed concerns over newly introduced technologies, such as yield-seeking AI agents that could threaten the deposit base of the biggest banks such as Citigroup (C) and Wells Fargo (WFC). “The death of large banks has been exaggerated for 50 years,” he said. “Their deposit franchises have become bigger over time, and the reason is trust. Trust is more important than Major Tech.”.

This trust in established financial institutions, along with massive banks’ aversion to risk in general, are likely to serve the banks especially well at a time of mounting unease over cybersecurity—the result of a spate of recent incidents, including ones involving rogue AI agents. In this context, the “goliath” banks may draw investors looking for a safe and steady play.

And while their performance trailed the broader S&P 500 in 2026, the Big Four banks delivered on another attribute that investors value: large and reliable dividends.

It has been revealed that it’s been about four years since OpenAI’s launch of ChatGPT set off a massive rally in AI stocks. Some investors are getting jitters about the scope of the AI build-out amid fears that it’s a bubble—especially after the blue wave midterms elected a slew of Democrats on promises to rein in the AI industry. Still, the tech behemoths at the center of the boom—including Meta Platforms, Microsoft, and Amazon—are going full speed.

In this environment, looking for opportunities is not about deciding whether artificial intelligence is the future (spoiler alert: It is). The real question is which companies are positioned to succeed, no matter the pace of the AI build-out.

Industry observers note that in this context, Bernstein senior analyst Stacy Rasgon likes the chipmaker Broadcom (AVGO) because its stock is “very, very cheap,” he told Fortune. The stock, like that of other chipmakers, sold off sharply in late 2026 as investors questioned how long the AI spending frenzy can last, even though earnings expectations remain strong.

Fellow chipmaker Nvidia’s shares took a major hit in November following revelations that its CEO, Jensen Huang, had acknowledged an affair, while the firm opened an investigation into reports that he had been targeted by Chinese intelligence. Huang resigned from the company he cofounded four days later.

Sources indicate that applied Materials (AMAT) is another stock that may offer considerable upside. The company sells equipment to manufacture chips, positioning Applied Materials to benefit from infrastructure investments in advanced processors, memory, and chip packaging. “It’s very clear to me that we need a lot more equipment,” mentioned Rasgon.

According to recent reports, that doesn’t mean these companies won’t face potential headwinds in 2027. Arun Sundaram, an investment strategist at CFRA, points to potential energy bottlenecks and concerns that higher interest rates could make AI financing more expensive. He cites political pushback against data center construction as another potential obstacle—opposition that will only increase as Democrats, many of whom have been vocal critics of the AI industry, take power in Congress.

It has been revealed that still, analysts like Rasgon remain optimistic. He pointed to third-quarter earnings from Major Tech, which included more AI spending and a surge in cloud revenues. “As it turns out, a lot of these companies may be more profitable than people thought. They’re actually generating money,” he mentioned. “From a fundamental level, we’ll probably see sustainability in spending … Whether or not sentiment from a stock standpoint is going to buy into that or not, I don’t know yet. But that’s going to be the key debate.”.

Industry observers note that most of our recommendations point you toward stocks or sectors to buy. When it comes to the defense industry in 2027 you might be well served to do the opposite: Stay on the sidelines. Russia’s invasion of Ukraine dragged into its fifth year in February 2026. That same month, the U.S. and Israel rolled out a war against Iran, triggering retaliatory attacks across the Middle East. By early summer, there was anxious talk in Washington, D.C., about depleted stocks of missiles and other munitions.

It has been revealed that in such an environment, investors might expect the shares of large defense companies to be soaring. That’s not the case. Even as demand for weapons has grown and a slew of techy startups have entered the sector, the stock prices of the significant military contractors known as the “primes”—including RTX, Northrop Grumman, and General Dynamics—have largely flailed. Only one of these companies, Lockheed Martin, outperformed the S&P. Shares of Boeing, which has a sizable division that sells to the military, lagged the index by 30%.

High interest rates are glum news for homebuyers and the real estate and AI industries, but individual savers and substantial banks can benefit—up to a point.

The reason for this lackluster performance is ongoing uncertainty over U.S. defense spending, said Peter Arment, a senior analyst at Baird. While the Pentagon and President Donald Trump are keen to pass a massive allocation for the military, it’s unclear where the money to pay for it would come from. Meanwhile, many in the incoming freshman class of Democrats vocally oppose Trump’s military policies.

While there is a tradition of bipartisan support for the military in Congress, this may not translate into a major defense bill in 2027, Arment remarked. Instead, lawmakers may rely on ad hoc measures that don’t include significant military spending.

We’ve all heard the buzz about GLP-1s, the blockbuster category of drugs that are delivering dramatic results in treating obesity and Type 2 diabetes. In 2027, the medications—sold under brand names including Ozempic and Wegovy—are poised to reach even more patients as insurance coverage expands and pills offer an alternative to injections.

JPMorgan forecasts that the global market for incretin-based drugs, which include GLP-1s, will reach $200 billion by 2030. In the U.S., the bank predicts that the number of patients taking these drugs will jump from roughly 10 million in 2025 to 25 million by the end of the decade.

This rise will be driven in part by expanded Medicare access. The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge, which released in July and runs through December 2027, offers certain weight-management drugs for $50 a month.

Sources indicate that GLP-1 in pill form could draw more users, too. Novo Nordisk’s oral Wegovy won FDA approval in December 2025, followed by Eli Lilly’s Foundayo in April 2026. Both are taken daily and could appeal to people who have held off on the treatment because they don’t like injections.

Lilly (LLY) and Novo (NVO) stocks stand to benefit the most. Both sell injectable and oral weight-loss treatments, and have spent years building the manufacturing facilities needed to meet demand. Lilly has committed more than $50 billion to U.S. manufacturing since 2020. It would take years for smaller would-be rivals to reach this scale. That business “moat” should help Lilly and Novo hold on to their lead, Evan Seigerman, BMO’s head of health care research, told Fortune: “I think that those two are poised to really maintain the lion’s share of the market in 2027,” he remarked. “You don’t see anyone else coming to take that share.”.

For investors looking for a picks-and-shovels play outside of the drugmakers themselves, West Pharmaceutical Services (WST) is an option. The manufacturer sells injectable-drug components like stoppers, plungers, and seals. Wall Street has taken notice: In November, Jefferies called the stock a buy and hiked its price target.

Industry observers note that those who assumed the solar sector was dead are missing out on one of the more surprising twists of 2027. Amid ongoing tensions in the Middle East, demand for energy is stronger than ever, and that is good news for solar power.

In a recent development, solar companies are also poised to benefit from developers rushing to meet a key end-of-2027 deadline for federal clean-electricity tax credits. The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 established the clean-electricity tax credits, but President Donald Trump’s 2025 One Massive Beautiful Bill Act accelerated their expiration. Projects that began construction after July 4, 2026, must be placed in service by the end of 2027; those that began construction on or before that date can qualify even if they come online later, subject to other requirements. The investment credit generally covers 30% of qualifying costs for projects, with additional bonuses available. Developers can alternatively claim a credit based on electricity production.

A rush by solar installers to meet the end-of-2027 deadline is likely to boost sales for First Solar (FSLR), which makes electricity-generating panels, and for Nextpower (NXT) and Array Technologies (ARRY), which sell tracking systems that help panels follow the sun.

Regardless of how many installers meet the solar tax credit deadline, overall energy consumption will rise in 2027. UBS projects this will lead to 310 gigawatts of combined U.S. solar and wind additions through 2030, driven partly by power-hungry data centers and industrial customers. Goldman Sachs forecasts global data center power demand will rise 220% from 2023 levels by 2030.

Natural gas could help meet that demand, but there has been a surge in orders for the gas turbines that power data centers, meaning delivery can take years. Case in point: GE Vernova, a leading maker of this heavy-duty machinery, was already taking orders for 2031 in July 2026.

Those long lead times could give solar an opening. Gregory Nemet, a professor at the University of Wisconsin, told Fortune that developers planning data centers in the next few years may choose solar if they cannot get these turbines. “That dynamic is pretty consequential to how fast solar grows,” Nemet said.

This article appears in the December 2026/January 2027 issue of Fortune.

It has been revealed that inflation remains stubborn. Producer prices are now running at a 6.5% annual clip, and affordability is top of mind. Want to cut some costs in your business? Of course you do. Try these moves.

Both ChatGPT and Claude offer connections to your bank account and credit card services. Or, if you’re nervous about that, just upload your statements. You’ll be impressed by the number of suggestions they make to reduce your spending and better manage expenses.

I used to think canceling online subscriptions would be a big headache, and years ago it was. Not anymore. Search for “cancel my subscription on Google Play” (or Apple or Amazon), and you’ll get direct links to do it. I’m betting you and your business have subscriptions you’ve forgotten about that are eating up hundreds of dollars a year.

Every year, put your business and auto insurance policies out for a quote. Ask your AI chatbot to make suggestions too. This is not very time-consuming and can be accomplished using an administrative person in your office. We’re oftentimes too lazy to do this. And that’s costing us.

It has been revealed that many of my clients have complicated, expensive coffee machines in their break rooms with a wide variety of coffees. They also stock sugar packets, teas, mini creamers, plastic stirrers and paper cups. It’s too much. Offer fewer coffees so you order less. Put out a sugar bowl, bring in a gallon of creamer and go back to ceramic mugs. Call me Scrooge, but it saves money.

According to recent reports, nerdWallet does a great job regularly reviewing business and personal credit cards. Again, use your AI chatbot to look at your spending and tell it your preferences and you’ll get plenty of recommendations too. Moving to a better card could earn you more points and cashback rewards then you’re getting right now. I have some clients that regularly switch back and forth.

Sources indicate that speaking of credit, if your business buys products on Amazon, then make sure you use one of Amazon’s credit cards for purchases. With a Prime membership, you can earn 5% back on eligible Amazon purchases, and there’s no annual fee.

If you can’t pay off a credit card purchase right away from operations, consider using working capital or a lower-rate loan to reduce the balance. Credit card interest rates are high, so this can cut what you pay in interest significantly.

This is a very common tax move, yet so many of us ignore it. Put as much as you can into your retirement strategy to lower your tax bill this year. When you save – assuming you’re eligible – sock money into a Roth IRA or Roth 401K so your after-tax money grows tax-free. With a Roth, there are no minimum distributions, and you can take the money out whenever you want, provided it meets certain requirements like a first-time home purchase, higher education or unreimbursed medical expenses.

Make sure your company has an HSA and contribute the max. It will reduce your tax expense and allow you to save money for future healthcare expenses.

Every square foot your inventory takes up costs you in overhead and space. Twice a year, take a hard look at your inventory and get rid of what isn’t moving. Sell it on Craigslist, eBay or Facebook Marketplace or scrap it.

Mark Cuban’s Cost Plus Drugs and Amazon Pharmacy both offer options that let businesses provide discounted prescription drugs, and they work with many popular health looks.

According to recent reports, set up a donor-advised fund and contribute to it this year, even if you haven’t decided which charities or nonprofits will receive the money. You take the deduction now and choose the recipients later.

It has been revealed that I like Capital One Shopping. Add it as a browser extension for yourself and anyone else who makes purchases for your business. Whenever someone is on a shopping site, it searches for available coupons before you buy. It works about half the time, and it has saved me significant money over the years.

It has been revealed that we can all afford the things we want — it’s just that sometimes we choose to spend our money on other things instead. That’s fine. But know that cutting back on things like travel, entertainment, subscriptions, marketing or other discretionary spending in your business (and your personal life) can help you reallocate your cash for other purposes. You’re more in control than you think.

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

AKT stakers are close to approving Akash's move from Cosmos to Solana, with Mintscan projecting a pass at 97.2% yes as voting enters its final hours.

Recent findings suggest that but a yes on Proposal 346 opens a door rather than completing a move. Before a single AKT reaches Solana, two independent audits and at least two more on-chain votes still have to happen.

The summary going around is simple: Akash is leaving Cosmos for Solana. The proposal itself is narrower than that, and the details matter for anyone holding AKT.

Industry observers note that proposal 346 on akashnet-2, titled "Migrate the Akash Protocol to Solana," closes at 15:02 UTC on November 2. A yes vote approves the migration plan and authorises AKT to launch as an SPL token through a one-way portal that stays open for two years. It does not set a cutover date, it does not move a single lease, and on its own it does not open the portal.

Sources indicate that the technical spec for that portal was published the day after voting opened. It demonstrates how many further steps lie between this vote and a working SPL AKT.

The proposal text in Akash's AEP repository says a yes vote does two things:.

It also claims plainly what it doesn't do: "it does not set a cutover date and does not move the marketplace." Live leases, staking and governance on akashnet-2 continue as normal. The marketplace moves only after audits and rehearsals pass and "a separate cutover proposal passes on this chain.".

A no vote would stop the whole plan. In the proposal's words: "Nothing moves; the token does not launch and the program returns to option analysis.".

At 08:43 UTC on November 2, about six hours before voting closed, Mintscan's page for Proposal 346 indicated an expected result of "Will PASS":.

In a recent development, turnout stood at 68.80% of bonded stake, against a quorum of 33.40%. The same figures can be read from Akash's own chain API, through the proposal object and its tally endpoint.

Mintscan's 97.2% is yes as a share of all votes cast. Akash's pass threshold leaves abstentions out, and on that basis yes stands at about 98.7%, far above the 50% needed. The veto share is negligible.

The tally has barely changed since early morning. A read of the chain at 07:29 UTC showed almost exactly the same totals, with only a handful of AKT added to the yes side. With turnout and margin that large, the outcome is not in doubt. The more useful question is what happens after it passes.

It has been revealed that the portal's design is in AEP-95, "One-Way AKT Sink to Solana,", a draft published on October 27 by core developers Artur Troian and Joseph Chalabi. It describes a "deliberately one-way" bridge with no return path. The authors say this removes "the largest class of bridge attacks.".

Why supply doesn't change: every SPL AKT is backed by AKT locked on Akash, and nothing is minted independently on Solana. The token is a legacy SPL mint with six decimals and no freeze authority.

The spec's own risk table names the biggest trust point. The upgrade authority over the Solana programs could "mint without limit." That power is meant to sit with a time-locked multisig appointed by Akash governance, with monitors set to alert on every admin action.

Industry observers note that at launch, SPL AKT has no protocol role. It will support "transfers and DEX liquidity only, with no staking or governance rights." Inflation stays on Akash. To seed trading, Overclock Labs, Akash's core developer, will send 1 million AKT through the bridge to a Solana treasury vault. That deposit follows the same rules as everyone else's.

In a recent development, proposal 346 requires "two independent audits of the token and portal code before launch," with reports published within 30 days. AEP-95's launch sequence indicates what that requirement means on-chain.

Sources indicate that so Proposal 346 is the first of at least five on-chain decisions. The "2 to 3 weeks" launch estimate depends on the audits finishing and the upgrade and parameter votes passing on schedule.

It has been revealed that for now, nothing. The proposal's disclosures set out what changes later:.

Discussion of the proposal continues in GitHub Discussion #1123.

The proposal lists four items as "still open, to be settled and published before the cutover proposal":.

It has been revealed that the second item matters most to holders. The portal closes two years after launch, and the proposal doesn't yet say what happens to AKT that hasn't crossed by then. The final tally will confirm whether the proposal goes ahead, but that answer, and the decisions in the votes that follow, will matter more to most holders than today's margin.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ripple’s longtime CTO emeritus David Schwartz does not think institutions can privately snap up billions of XRP via dark pools without affecting the token’s price on public markets.
  • According to recent reports, "I don't think so.
  • This was in response to a question posed by an XRP community member wondering if private trading platforms might give institutions an advantage over retail investors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ripple’s longtime CTO emeritus David Schwartz does not think institutions can privately snap up billions of XRP via dark pools without affecting the token’s price on public markets.

According to recent reports, "I don't think so. Who are they buying the XRP from? Why wouldn't people generally want the price to rise when they buy? But it's not impossible," Schwartz wrote on X on Nov. 24.

This was in response to a question posed by an XRP community member wondering if private trading platforms might give institutions an advantage over retail investors.

Earlier in the conversation, Schwartz noted the pros and cons of dark pools for retail traders.

In a recent development, he mentioned one disadvantage: less efficient price discovery. Given that bids and offers are obscured, retail traders in public markets have less insight into other traders’ bids and ask prices.

According to recent reports, if there is a large XRP holder who is already inclined to sell at the current price, an institution could arrange a private trade with this holder without needing to place a massive buy order on an exchange. They could execute the trade without driving the public price up as they buy.

Industry observers note that however, will there be enough sellers interested in offloading billions of XRP like this? One might run out of sellers willing to sell at that price. So, the buyer might need to up the ante to find the next willing seller.

A dark pool can hide order size, but one still needs someone on the other side to execute that order.

Plus, a buyer will naturally prefer not to tip its hand while accumulating a position.

Schwartz left open the possibility of a private purchase at scale, but the possibility is rather low.

Recent findings suggest that when asked why XRP Ledger developments were not doing anything for XRP’s price on Nov. 9, Schwartz pointed to the broader crypto market.

He also debunked the notion that Ripple had some secret initiative it was not sharing with holders. The tech giant regularly talks about its aims.

Schwartz also mentioned a practical benefit of XRP being worth more in the: a higher price could mean cheaper liquidity provision and less slippage (the difference between the expected price a trader pays and the price they actually pay).

At the same time, he was less convinced that demand for XRP to pay transaction fees could have a big impact on the price by itself.
